News.title: Horror moment sightseeing helicopter plunges to ground and crash-lands on two tourists at popular scenic spot
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a sightseeing helicopter plunges to the ground and crashes on top of fleeing tourists.

Two people miraculously survived being crushed after the gyroplane started to spin wildly out of control in the air and landed on top of them.



Shocking footage shows the yellow helicopter performing a routine low-altitude demonstration flight as part of a three-aircraft formation over a lake in China.

Huge plumes of smoke begin pouring out of the back of the aircraft as it rapidly loses altitude and drops towards dozens of beachgoers below.



As it approaches the ground, the pilot appears to try and wrestle back control but causes the helicopter to suddenly spin around.

Within seconds it smashed into the ground and landed directly on top of two tourists.



The victims watched on in terror as they tried to run away but the heavy aircraft plowed straight into them.

Both were knocked over and sustained serious head injuries.



Those inside the Harbin XLI gyroplane escaped injury and immediately helped those on the ground.

The crash happened at Chaka Sky No. 1 Scenic Area beside the salt lake in Qinghai Province on Tuesday, July 21.

The tourists remained conscious as they were rushed to hospital.

They were first taken to Ulan County People’s Hospital before being transferred to a larger facility in Haixi Prefecture.

Officials from the Ulan County Joint Investigation Group said: “A self-rotating rotorcraft crash-landed, injuring two people on the ground.



“The victims were sent for medical treatment at the first opportunity.

“Their vital signs are currently stable.”

The aircraft has been seized as investigations continue into what caused the accident at the scenic beauty spot.

Early indications suggest wake turbulence from a nearby gyroplane may have triggered the pilot’s loss of control.

News.title: Chef, 28, who suddenly disappeared in early hours two weeks ago is found dead in woodland
News.content:
CHEF TRAGEDY Chef, 28, who suddenly disappeared in early hours two weeks ago is found dead in woodland

A CHEF has been found dead in a city park after suddenly disappearing more than two weeks ago.

Dener Marcos Guieiro, 28, was last seen in the early hours of July 4 after leaving for work.



Following his disappearance the Met Police issued a missing persons appeal.

A picture of Dener was shared online with the hopes that he could be located.



Cops said they were growing concerned for his welfare as they appealed for the public’s help locating the Brazilian Chef.

Tragically, Dener’s family have now confirmed that his body was discovered in a park in Hackney, London, on July 18.

It is understood that Dener’s body had been left undiscovered in a wooded area of the park for two weeks.

Police later told the chef’s relatives that CCTV footage had shown him getting into his car carrying his wallet and a black briefcase before he disappeared.

The Metropolitan Police confirmed officers had found the body of a man matching Mr Guieiro’s description on July 18.

Formal identification is yet to take place and an exact cause of death has not been disclosed.



Originally from Belo Horizonte in Brazil, the 28-year-old had lived in Hackney for six years before he disappeared.

His twin sister, Ana Luiza Guieiro, said cops had contacted Dener’s family in Brazil to inform them of the discovery.

In an online fundraising appeal she wrote: “My twin brother passed away in London, far from home, family and everyone who loved him.

“Beyond the immeasurable pain of this loss, we are facing a challenge that is beyond our financial means – bringing his body back to Brazil so we can say goodbye with dignity and allow him to rest alongside those who always loved him.

“Every contribution, regardless of the amount, brings us closer to this final act of love.



“If you can’t help financially, sharing this campaign will also make a huge difference.”

The Sun has contacted the Metropolitan Police for comment.

News.title: New hosepipe ban now in force for 10MILLION customers – check six rules you cannot break
News.content:
THE UK’s biggest water supplier has enforced a hosepipe ban for 10million customers this morning, as eight UK regions edge closer to drought.

The ban takes the total number of Brits under restrictions to 23million, with the majority coming into force in the South of England.



Thames Water has introduced a temporary hosepipe ban to 10million of its drinking water customers.

From 00.01am this morning, regions across London, Thames Valley, Surrey, Gloucestershire, Kent, and Essex came under restrictions.



On Tuesday, when the restrictions were announced, the water company said: “A temporary hosepipe ban has been announced for customers who receive their water supply from Thames Water.

“We’ve been working around the clock to maintain water supplies, but we now need everyone’s help to reduce non-essential water use.



“Customers affected by the ban are expected to follow the restrictions while it remains in place.”

Now, 23million people across England and Wales are currently under hosepipe ban restrictions, with seven water companies rolling out these measures.

Under a temporary use ban, customers cannot use a hosepipe, sprinkler, or pressure washer for various activities, such as watering plants, or filling up hot tubs.



Anyone caught breaking the rules imposed by the water supplier can face a £1,000 fine.

This is not the case, however, if an approved exemption is in place, with a number of loopholes meaning you can still look after your garden.

Even under a hosepipe ban, newly-laid garden turf can be watered for 28 days, new trees and saplings can be tended to, and a watering can may still be used.

Any hosepipe use is also permitted when it concerns the welfare, safety, and health of people and animals, with Blue Badge holders and individuals on the Priority Services Register all exempt.

The introduction comes as the Environment Agency warns that much of England has moved closer to drought status following an unprecedented third heatwave of the year.



Hosepipe ban rules - what you can't use a hose for The rules of a hosepipe ban: No watering gardens using hoses or sprinklers

No cleaning cars, boats or other motor vehicles

No watering plants on domestic land

No filling or maintaining domestic swimming or paddling pools

No filling domestic ponds or fountains

No cleaning outdoor surfaces like patios, walls or paths

Eight regions across the UK have now been classified as having “prolonged dry weather” areas, including London, with six reservoirs classed as having “notably low” water levels.

Thames Water customers have been using an extra 100 million litres of water every day to combat the hot temperatures, adding on to the 2.5billion litres of drinking water the company supplies already.

Earlier this week, South East Water announced that 2.4million more of its customers would come under restrictions, with homes across Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire and Berkshire now impacted by the change.

Anglian Water, Affinity Water, Cambridge Water, Southern Water, South West Water and Welsh Water have also introduced bans to customers.

Thames Water has not yet confirmed how long this temporary hosepipe ban will last for its customers, just that it will stay in place “until water levels recover.”



If your water supplier is affected, it is important to check their website to find out if your postcode is impacted by the changes.

News.title: I escaped the manosphere – the arrest of the Tate brothers won’t end the dark lure of toxic masculinity and here’s why
News.content:
'MATRIX ATTACK' I escaped the manosphere – the arrest of the Tate brothers won’t end the dark lure of toxic masculinity and here’s why

THE charges faced by Andrew Tate could hardly be more serious – multiple rapes, sex trafficking and possessing indecent images of children.

In total, police in Britain have accused the influencer and his younger brother Tristan of 59 offences, with the authorities in Romania also investigating the pair for organised crime.



Yet, after their arrest in Miami at the weekend, their devoted followers continue to praise the brothers who grew up in Luton, Bedfordshire.

Most of the discussion on social media was about the silk purple shirt and penny loafers Andrew, 39, was wearing as federal agents handcuffed him in the bright Florida sunshine.



It is nearly four years since the duo were first arrested in Romania on sex trafficking allegations.

Rather than curtailing the two men, it only seems to have boosted the profile of the Tates, who continue to promote their alpha male brand with a depressing swagger.

Andrew was due to host a bareknuckle boxing event when he was nabbed in Miami and last year lost a lucrative Misfits boxing match.

He posts clips of himself on private jets, with fast cars and girls and snarls: “Put us in jail, we don’t care.”

A couple of weeks ago, Tristan, 38, used a racist term during a long rant on their Tate Speech videocast, saying “I am innocent. I am not scared of these n******”.

All this bravado is lapped up by the so-called manosphere.



The vital message delivered by the award-winning Adolescence Netflix series- deaths of women at the hands of brainwashed young men and constant warnings that dangerous sexual activities such as strangulation have become normalised- has done little to dent this cult-like movement.

As Louis Theroux’s recent documentary about the manosphere revealed, there are plenty of other influencers jostling for attention.

One man who was lured in by the Tates’ messages, but came out the other side, tells The Sun we need to tackle the problems facing teenage men to prevent them spreading.

James Blake, who made the BBC documentary Men of the Manosphere, says: “If you’re a 15 or 16-year-old boy repeatedly seeing content telling you that men are the problem or that you’re somehow less valuable because of your sex, it’s understandable that some will seek out communities that make them feel seen and validated instead.

“That doesn’t excuse misogyny or harmful rhetoric, but if we genuinely want to reduce the influence of extreme voices, we have to ask why so many young men feel they need to look elsewhere for that sense of belonging in the first place.



“Tackling only the symptoms without addressing those underlying issues won’t solve the problem.”

The Tates’ central idea that if you want to have sex you need to project wealth certainly seems to have taken hold.

Last autumn a YouGov poll revealed that almost a third of Millennial men believe that women only want to date males of a “high social status.”



The manosphere was built on sex.

Many of the alpha males in this online world started as pick-up artists, offering to show other males how to attract women.

The Tates charged for courses which taught members “how to obtain and retain unlimited beautiful women.”

And a key member of his organisation, an American called Miles Sonkin, claimed in the 1990s to be the “world’s greatest pick-up artist”.

It was in May of 2014 that the public started to become aware of the manosphere, a malevolent force that had been gaining traction in the darker recesses of the internet.



London-born Elliot Rodger, 22, murdered six people and injured 14 others in a mass shooting in California, where he had lived since the age of five.

Rodger, who shot himself after the killing spree, was a frustrated pick-up artist spreading hatred of the opposite sex. He wanted “a world where women fear you.”

Similar attacks have followed, including 22–year–old incel Jake Davison, who shot five people dead in Plymouth before taking his own life in 2021.



Andrew Tate has denied being part of the manosphere. Instead, he claims to promote the idea of strong, independent men.

In the early 2020s, following a break-up with his girlfriend, James shared some of Tate’s social media messages.

James recalls: “Like many people, I first came across Andrew Tate through short-form clips on Instagram and other social media.

“My initial impression was that he mixed conventional self-improvement advice, discipline, fitness, confidence and ambition.

“The content over time, however, became more polarising and more relationship-focused. I could understand why some young men found parts of the messaging appealing, even if I disagreed with other aspects of it.”



Having left that world, James made a documentary last year about the manosphere, in which he interviewed men drawn to an anti-women agenda.

He continues: “What interested me during the process of making my BBC documentary, Men of the Manosphere, wasn’t simply Andrew Tate or other individuals themselves, but understanding why so many young men were receptive to that message in the first place.

“Loneliness, a lack of positive role models, struggles with dating, uncertainty about masculinity and a desire for purpose all played a role.

“The content made by influencers from both genders and sometimes the media which portrays all men as bad or not good enough, doesn’t help.”

Tate, who was also a kickboxer and ran a webcam business, moved to Romania in 2015, where the brothers have a compound with a fleet of flash cars.



Both Andrew and Tristan have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

Following their arrest this weekend, their lawyer Joseph McBride put out a statement claiming the charges were “a political hit ordered by a dying empire.”

The brothers are being held in custody and will fight attempts to have them extradited from the US to the UK.

Tristan says he has told prosecutors in Romania that they shouldn’t take all his previous statements about his sexual behaviour seriously.

Before his most recent arrest, Tristan told followers in a video that “I am playing a character, relax, this is a joke”.



Online, the pair still have plenty of support from people who believe they have taken a “red pill” – a reference to the sci-fi film The Matrix – which makes them aware of a conspiracy.

James explains: “From what I observe, some people think the arrest of Andrew Tate is a ‘Matrix Attack’ or some kind of attack from a deep ‘system that controls us.’

“Others simply believe he should be presumed innocent until proven guilty. Equally, many former supporters have distanced themselves following the allegations.”



There is some evidence that the influence of the Tates might be waning.

In 2023, 27 per cent of 18- 29-year-old men had a favourable view of Andrew Tate. Three years later, only 13 per cent of Generation Z, which is that age group, felt the same.

But if anyone thinks that signals the beginning of the end of what many regard as toxic masculinity, they’d be mistaken.

Privately educated Essex-born Harrison Sullivan built up a major following by saying outrageous things on social media.

Operating under the name HSTikkytokky, he said: “Call me racist, call me a misogynist, call me homophobic, call me a scammer – I’m all those things.”



Sullivan was the main subject of Louis Theroux’s Inside the Manosphere documentary for Netflix earlier this year.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But James believes the success of the toxic influencers is a symptom and not the cause.

James concludes: “There will always be more creators. Too much of the conversation focuses on individual influencers and not enough on why millions of young men around the world are looking for them in the first place.”

News.title: Sick arsonists tie fuel-soaked rags to CATS to spread horror wildfires in Italy as Europe’s tourist hotspots burn
News.content:
TWISTED arsonists have been accused of tying “fuel-soaked rags” to the tails of cats and setting them on fire, sparking major wildfires in Italy.

Strays are believed to have had flammable material wrapped around them which is set alight as the animals run away in fear spreading the fire.



Domenico Costarella of Calabria’s Civil Protection Agency claimed: “These animals were released into the fields, running around and spreading the fire.”

The Italian Association for the Defense of Animals and the Environment has now filed a criminal complaint, according to SkyTG24.





A 1,000 euro (£858) reward for information on who may have set the cats alight has also been announced.

No arrests have been made in connection to the feline abuse yet.



Using pets for notorious means has been seen in Italy in the past.

Back in 2016, the Italian mafia were accused of using cats to spread forest fires and a year later officials accused the mob of the same tactic to spark blazes outside of Naples.

The current fires raging across Europe are believed to have been significantly amplified by the hot weather and high winds in recent weeks, resulting in dry crops and woodlands.

Wildfires have swept across parts of Italy, France and Spain all on Wednesday, with three firefighters killed and thousands forced to evacuate their homes.

In Sicily, around 6,000 firefighters, forest guards and civil protection officials battled dozens of fires across the Mediterranean island.



A spokesperson for the Italian Civil Protection Agency called the situation “serious” and warned the fires are “being fuelled by very high temperatures and very dry soil”.

More than 160 fires have also been recorded in the neighbouring Calabria region.

The head of local civil protection blamed the fires on “malicious individuals” – including people using the stray cats.



Regional president Renato Schifani said 50 fires were still burning as of Thursday morning as water-bombing aircraft continue to fight the flames.

Across in France, two firefighters died while tackling a blaze that broke out near Bordeaux airport.

Firefighting unions have warned workers are facing “exhaustion” and a lack of resources.

Firefighter Captain Wilfried Schneider said: “We’re dealing with a very dense stand of closely packed pines.”

Two fires displaced thousands of people in the country’s southwest as the inferno ravaged nearly 5,000 acres in the picturesque Arcachon Basin region.



In total, 12,000 people have been evacuated in southwest France with major warnings still in place.

How to stay safe if you're around a wildfire THE British Red Cross advice for how to stay safe in the event of a wildfire is as follows: If you see a wildfire and are outside: Stay calm

Ensure you are in a safe location (away from vegetation and smoke)

If you are in your car, close all windows and vents

Call emergency services immediately. Tell the fire control the location, size, and any relevant information including the address, OS, or What3Words location. If you are at home: Stay calm

Put yourself in a place of safety – do not try to put out the fire yourself

Keep doors and windows closed but unlocked

Call emergency services immediately and inform them of your location. Provide them with as much detail as possible. Including the address, OS or What3Words location.

and inform them of your location. Provide them with as much detail as possible. Including the address, OS or What3Words location. Let them know the best access point to get to the property. If safe to do so, stand by the access point and speak to fire crews when they arrive. When driving through wildfire smoke: Motorists who have to travel through the smoke should: Keep windows closed, turn off air conditioning, and keep their air vents closed

Smoke can irritate air passages, skin, and eyes, resulting in coughing and wheezing, breathlessness, and chest pain

Individuals with pre-existing cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, such as asthma, should carry any necessary medication or inhalers with them at all times and seek medical advice if their symptoms worsen

One of the worst blazes hit Le Porge and has ripped through 4,900 acres since Wednesday, officials said.

Dramatic footage from France shows a “fire tornado” spreading across a field.

Also known as a fire whirl, the phenomenon forms when hot air released by a fire encounters particular air movements which cause it to rotate at speed.

Spain has also been fighting the flames as authorities ordered the evacuation of several districts on Wednesday around the city of Toledo, south of Madrid.



Several roads were cut off sparking travel chaos as the Civil Guard tried to get people to safety as multiple fires broke out near homes.

Spain has been gripped by a spate of wildfires this summer, including one of its deadliest in recent memory, where 13 people were killed in the southern province of Almeria.

Seven Brits – including a 93-year-old woman – died in the blaze that consumed 7,000 hectares of land.

Hundreds of firefighters are still battling a large wildfire in Guadalajara province, around 100 kilometres north of Madrid.

It has burnt through about 79,000 hectares since it started last Thursday.

News.title: Asylum seeker who knocked woman unconscious after she rejected his advances on night out is jailed for just six months
News.content:
A SICK asylum seeker who knocked a woman unconscious after she rejected him has been jailed for just six months – as the victim’s mum slammed his sentence.

Abdoela Berhan sent 20-year-old Cleo Lake crashing to the ground with a single punch while on a night out.



The 35-year-old had ambushed Cleo and her friends as they left a nightclub in Bournemouth, Dorset.

She had told Eritrean national Berhan to “f**k off” and pushed him away when he got in her personal space.



The footage, which has been released by the CPS, showed the hotel migrant aiming a kick at the young woman, who retaliated.

Berhan then pulled his left arm back and punched Cleo in the face – knocking her unconscious before fleeing.

When he was later arrested Berhan, whose address was given as the taxpayer-funded Britannia migrant hotel, claimed he acted in self-defence.

Cleo, who suffered a broken nose in the attack, described the harrowing footage as “hard to watch”.



Berhan failed to turn up for court but was found guilty of the assault in his absence – just one week after he was also convicted of a rampage in Subway.

He was also found guilty of criminal damage to a police cell following a trial.

Cleo’s mum Helen O’Brien has now slammed Berhan as a “disgusting human being” as he was jailed for just six months.

She said: “Six months doesn’t seem long enough.

“The impact of leaving Cleo in a crumpled bloody mess in that alley has lasted more than six months for us.



“I still cry when I think about that CCTV showing what he did to her and Cleo is still not the happy carefree girl she once was.

“The cheek of him to still deny it when it’s there in black and white just goes to show what a disgusting human being he is. He’s clearly not remorseful at all.

“I hope his time in prison teaches him a hard lesson. I just wish he would have got more time. He’ll probably be out earlier than six months.”



The attack took place in the early hours of December 7, 2024.

Cleo and her friends, who had been to the Cameo nightclub, were outside eating some food when Berhan approached them.

She told Poole Magistrates’ Court: “He tried to sit down with us, I got uncomfortable because none of us knew who he was, it was dark and there was no-one else around.

“I told him to f**k off and he didn’t like it.

“We were arguing, swearing at each other and he got rather close so I shoved him back. He turned around and kicked me, but missed, then I kicked him.”



Cleo also bravely told how she did not go out much after the attack and had become anxious and “uncomfortable” around men.

She added: “Even now, a year and a half later, I won’t go out clubbing unless there’s a lot of us or someone’s boyfriend is there, for protection. Because I have the thought that something bad will kick off.”

Berhan fled after the attack but was found guilty in his absence – with a warrant issued for his arrest.



Speaking through a Tigrinyan interpreter, Berhan told Southampton Magistrates’ Court that Cleo had tried to intimidate him.

He said: “There were three girls, I approached them and asked them to give me a lighter. The one who was standing said ‘f**k off’ and tried to intimidate me. I was defending myself by my elbows.

“It was not my intention to attack her.”

But District Judge Orla Austin said she didn’t believe him and handed him the maximum sentence possible for assault.

She said: “You made advances to Miss Lake, which were rejected. She was entitled to reject your advances. She was a young woman.



“Your reaction was to punch her with significant force to the face. That blow rendered her unconscious, left her bleeding in the street and required the ambulance to attend.

“I’m satisfied a high level of violence was used against her. Though you say you were in some way defending yourself, the footage clearly shows otherwise.

“You denied all offences and put Miss Lake through a trial.

“In my judgement this is an exceptional case. There was very serious violence against a young woman who had simply rejected your advances.”

It comes after the thug was previously convicted for spitting and kicking at a Subway worker in Bournemouth.



Berhan lashed out at Sahjan Chowdhury when he tried to make him leave for being aggressive.

He fled the shop in Bournemouth, Dorset – only to return later that day to pick up food orders for his Just Eat delivery job.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Poole Magistrates’ Court heard the attack took place at around 4.50am on November 30, 2024, close to his asylum hotel.

Asked whether Berhan will be deported after serving his sentence, a Home Office spokesperson said: “Where a foreign national poses a threat to the UK, we will always seek to deport them.”

News.title: Brit found dead after locking himself in bedroom in Marbella flat while being evicted for failing to pay rent for 2yrs
News.content:
EVICTION TRAGEDY Brit found dead after locking himself in bedroom in Marbella flat while being evicted for failing to pay rent for 2yrs

A BRITISH man has been found dead after locking himself inside his rented Costa del Sol flat bedroom as authorities prepared to evict him.

The UK national, 40, was about to be kicked out of the Marbella property for not paying any rent over the last two years.



Spanish officials came to the house on Tuesday after getting the green light to take possession of it and hand the property back to its rightful owner.

The dwelling is located on a residential estate called Altos de Rodeo, a short walk from the upmarket port of Puerto Banus.



The Brit initially opened the door when the eviction team approached the apartment.

But he went back inside the home after asking for more time to gather his belongings.

The Brit reportedly locked the door of his bedroom from the inside and failed to come out again.

Police were called to the scene before they forcibly broke into the bedroom.

The unnamed Brit reportedly had several criminal convictions for theft, fraud and domestic violence, according to Spanish outlet El Mundo.

His passport had been confiscated because he was categorised as a potential flight risk, the newspaper reported.

It comes after a Brit fell to his death in a Costa del Sol hotel balcony after grieving the loss of his daughter.

Robert Davidson, 37, took his own life at the four-star Sandos Griego Hotel, in the popular resort of Torremolinos, his devastated fiancée said.

He had been on holiday with fiancée Daniella Robb, 27, and her two children.

She was asleep when her partner plummeted to his death from the balcony of their sixth-floor room, just before midnight on Tuesday.



Robert took his life hours before the first anniversary of the death of the couple’s daughter, Hollie.

She tragically died at just seven-weeks-old from Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS).

News.title: Millions 'walking around' with early sign of disease 'months before feeling ill'
News.content:
Millions 'walking around' with early sign of disease 'months before feeling ill'

A health expert has issued a warning over the early warning sign and what to do about it

View 3 Images Eye surgeon reveals signs that could warn you of the disease months before you feel ill (Image: Getty)

Millions of Brits could be 'walking around' with the early signs of a common disease 'staring back at them in the mirror', an eye surgeon has warned. In the UK, over two million people are affected by some form of serious liver disease, but as many as 70% of them are not diagnosed.

‌



Doctors say the eyes can flag trouble with the liver long before the classic symptoms of liver disease, including tiredness, nausea and stomach pain, ever appear - and often before a blood test. A major red flag is jaundice, a yellowing of the whites of the eyes caused when a struggling liver can no longer clear a waste product called bilirubin from the blood.

‌



Mr Allon Barsam, consultant eye surgeon and founding partner of OCL Vision, said the eyes can act as an early warning system for a disease that often develops silently. He explained: "The eyes are one of the few places on the body where we can actually see what is happening inside.

‌



"A yellow tinge to the whites of the eyes is one of the earliest visible clues that the liver may be in trouble, and it’s something people dismiss far too easily." It's not the only clue. Soft, yellowish cholesterol deposits on or around the eyelids, known as xanthelasma, can indicate chronic liver problems that prevent the body from processing fats properly.

A rare copper build-up linked to an inherited liver condition can leave faint brownish-gold rings around the coloured part of the eye. Some patients also notice their eyes becoming unusually dry, gritty or irritated, which can be linked to autoimmune forms of liver disease.

View 3 Images Yellow colouring can indicate chronic liver (stock image)

‌



Mr Barsam added: "If you notice yellowing, unusual deposits on the eyelids or persistent dryness, please do not wait. By the time serious liver damage shows up elsewhere, precious time may already have been lost. Catching these signs early can make an enormous difference."

Liver disease is a serious and growing problem in the UK. Unlike several other major health issues, the death rates are increasing, making it the second leading cause of death for people under 65 in England and Wales.

As many as 90% of these cases could be avoided. In England, there are over 82,000 hospital admissions each year due to liver disease. Anyone with any concerns or questions about their health or symptoms should speak to a GP.

‌



View 3 Images It is the second leading cause of death for people under 65 in England and Wales

The eye surgeon says much of the damage is preventable, and other experts stress that spotting it early gives patients the best chance of successful treatment. Mr Barsam urged anyone worried about changes to their eyes to see their GP or optician rather than assume it will pass.

"An eye test is about far more than checking your vision," he said. "Sometimes it can be the first step to catching a life-threatening illness in time."

News.title: The hidden health risk you face when getting in a car this summer
News.content:
The hidden health risk you face when getting in a car this summer

With temperatures growing ever higher as the sun continues to bake Britain, skin experts and the car industry are combining to issue important health advice for motorists

View 2 Images Sunburn is a real risk - even when in the car (Image: IMAGO Images / Cover Images)

Millions of Brits are unknowingly putting themselves at risk of sunburn every time they get behind the wheel.

‌



New research has found that 47% of motorists take no precautions against UV exposure despite an estimated 14million experiencing sunburn while travelling by car. Around one in three (31%) said they didn't even realise it was possible to get sunburnt inside a vehicle, according to the survey by Autotrader and the British Skin Foundation.

‌



While modern windscreens block the vast majority of UVB radiation, many side windows can still allow significant levels of UVA rays into the vehicle. Dr Zainab Laftah, consultant dermatologist and spokesperson for the British Skin Foundation, said: "A common misconception is that being inside a vehicle provides complete protection from the sun.

‌



View 2 Images Sunscreen should be part of the journey when you're travelling by road in sunny weather (Image: IMAGO Images / Cover Images)

UK weather maps show 7C bitter August chill after scorching 37C heatwave READ MORE :

Sir David Beckham pictured holidaying with Victoria in Ibiza after World Cup READ MORE :

“In reality, both short periods of intense UV exposure and repeated exposure over time contribute to an increased risk of skin cancer. While standard car windscreens block most UVB radiation, the amount of UVA that enters a vehicle varies depending on the type, thickness and tint of the glass.

“This means a significant amount of UVA can still penetrate vehicle windows, contributing to cumulative skin damage, premature skin ageing, pigmentation changes and an increased risk of skin cancer over time.”

‌



While UVB rays are those primarily responsible for sunburn, UVA rays can cause deep skin damage and heighten the risk of skin cancer. Dr Laftah’s warning comes as demand for open-top motoring rises with the temperature. During the May heatwave, searches for convertibles on Autotrader increased by 8 per cent week-on-week, with models including the Porsche 911, Mazda MX-5 and Mercedes-Benz SL among the most-viewed vehicles on the platform.

She said that those driving convertibles need to be even more wary - and take care they know how long they are spending in the sun. "Many drivers also underestimate how long they're exposed during everyday journeys, particularly on longer drives or when sitting in traffic,” she said.

“For drivers of convertibles and other open-top vehicles, the risk is even greater because the face, scalp, neck, arms and hands are exposed to direct sunlight for prolonged periods."

‌



The stark warning follows separate British Skin Foundation research from 2025 which found that a third of Brits had already been sunburnt by early summer. The same proportion (31%) admitted they simply "couldn't be bothered" to wear sunscreen in sunny weather.

Rory Reid, YouTube director at Autotrader, continued: "Nothing beats driving with the roof down on a sunny day, and every time the weather improves, we see demand for convertibles climb. What many people don't realise is that spending time behind the wheel can expose them to harmful UV rays, even inside the car.

“Whether you're driving to work, heading off on holiday or simply enjoying the sunshine, applying sunscreen should be as much a part of your journey as checking your tyre pressures, topping up your screen wash or making sure you've got water in the car."

‌

News.title: 'Trump’s Saudi nuclear deal reeks of hypocrisy - and demands answers'
News.content:
Donald Trump has just shattered what little moral authority America had left on nuclear weapons.

Washington has agreed a 30-year pact that could give Saudi Arabia access to the very technology Trump treats as an intolerable threat when Iran pursues it. America has gone to war, saying Tehran cannot be trusted with uranium enrichment, yet it is now offering a pathway towards it to a wealthy Gulf ally.

Apparently, uranium becomes less dangerous when it comes wrapped in money, flattery and the promise of lucrative business. Trump presents himself as the hardest man in any room, but in reality, he often looks like the easiest man in the world to buy. Praise him, roll out a red carpet, tell him he is a genius, and even the most serious questions of global security suddenly appear negotiable.

View 4 Images Trump’s deal with the Crown Prince could give Saudi Arabia access to uranium enrichment technology, raising questions over what America received in return (Image: Getty Images)

‌



That is what makes this deal so alarming. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has said his country would seek a nuclear weapon if Iran obtained one. A responsible president would therefore insist on the toughest inspections, the strongest safeguards and a firm ban on domestic enrichment.

Trump appears to have settled for something far easier: trust the Saudis, trust him and stop asking what may have been discussed behind closed doors.

At the very moment the Middle East is becoming more dangerous, Trump is weakening the safeguards designed to stop a nuclear arms race. Riyadh, meanwhile, appears to have understood the quickest route to his approval: praise, pageantry and profit.

The original offer of nuclear cooperation was supposed to come in return for Saudi Arabia establishing formal relations with Israel. The war in Gaza destroyed that prospect, yet Trump has handed Riyadh the nuclear prize anyway. Why? What did America receive in return? What was promised privately? And how long before Trump’s Tweedledee and Tweedledum sons, Don Jr or Eric, suddenly announce that uranium, reactor construction or Saudi infrastructure has always been a personal passion?

‌



That question is not frivolous. It goes to the heart of the problem with Trump’s presidency.

His family has repeatedly invested in industries shaped by decisions made by his administration. His gormless sons have put money into businesses linked to defence, drones, cryptocurrency and critical minerals, sectors that can benefit from US government contracts, public backing or favourable policy.

View 4 Images The Saudi agreement has fuelled fears of a fresh nuclear arms race across the Middle East. (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Each time, the explanation is the same. They are private businessmen. They are passive investors. They played no role in the decisions. What astonishing luck they continue to enjoy. Most presidents go to great lengths to avoid even the appearance that they can be bought. Trump appears more concerned that people might think he came cheaply.

‌



Congress must follow the money before this agreement goes any further. Which companies will build the reactors? Who owns them? Who invested before the agreement was signed? Which lobbyists met administration officials? Have Trump family businesses, funds, investors or partners held talks with Saudi figures or companies likely to benefit?

Have Don Jr or Eric acquired interests in businesses connected to nuclear energy, uranium, construction, technology or Saudi infrastructure? These questions exist because Trump has allowed conflicts of interest to become a permanent feature of his presidency. Public power and private profit now sit so closely together they may as well share a desk in the Oval Office.

Trump will inevitably dismiss scrutiny as a witch hunt. He prefers that phrase because “please show us the contracts” sounds rather less dramatic. Yet nuclear policy cannot be allowed to become another Trump family business opportunity whose true winners emerge only after the papers are signed and journalists begin searching company records.

View 4 Images Critics warn that allowing Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium would weaken efforts to stop nuclear weapons from spreading across the region (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The danger goes far beyond his family. A Saudi enrichment programme could encourage other regional powers to demand the same capability. Iran will argue that America’s nuclear rules depend entirely on whether a country is an enemy, an ally or a promising location for a Trump-branded development.

That charge will be difficult to dismiss. Trump boasts that he is the world’s greatest dealmaker. Increasingly, he resembles a man who will hand over the keys provided the buyer spends enough time admiring his ego.

A nuclear agreement cannot be treated like a casino licence, a hotel contract or another opportunity to put the family name above an entrance. If it goes wrong, the consequences cannot be covered with gold paint, dismissed as bad publicity or blamed on a former business partner.

Before Saudi Arabia enriches a single grain of uranium, Trump must reveal exactly what has been agreed, which businesses stand to gain and whether anyone connected to his family was anywhere near the negotiations. Because when the Trumps are involved, even nuclear non-proliferation risks becoming just another grift with gold lettering on the door.

News.title: Robert Jenrick faces calls to apologise for sharing 'doctored' comment by Labour minister
News.content:
Robert Jenrick faces calls to apologise for sharing 'doctored' comment by Labour minister

Reform's Robert Jenrick sparked anger by sharing a clip on social media suggesting Jo White said 'I don't care if we stop the boats'. Ms White shared a full clip in which she can be heard saying it is her 'number one priority'

Jo White reveals what she actually said about small boats

Reform's Robert Jenrick is under pressure to apologise after being accused of sharing a doctored quote from Labour's new migration minister to score points.

‌



The former Tory sparked outrage by posting a clip suggesting Jo White - who was announced as part of Shabana Mahmood's Home Office team on Wednesday - told constituents she dd not care about stopping small boats. Ms White later posted a full audio, making it clear she had said: "I don't care who will stop the boats... my number one priority is to stop those boats."

‌



In a post on X which was later deleted, Mr Jenrick claimed she had said: "I don't care if we stop the boats." And he claimed that Andy Burnham "clearly doesn't give a stuff about stopping the boats".

‌



On Thursday morning he said he had deleted the post, but denied he was wrong to post it.

View 2 Images Robert Jenrick faces calls to apologise (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

An outraged Ms White wrote posted a recording of her comments to constituents, saying: "Robert Jenrick is spreading a false account of what I said at a meeting with my constituents last year.

‌



"This recording proves what I said. Reform have deliberately twisted my words to mislead the public. They should withdraw their false claim and immediately apologise."

Mr Jenrick's post was deleted, but he has not posted an apology. Labour MP Jacob Collier posted: "In sharing a doctored audio clip of Jo, Jenrick and Reform are once again showing their desperation and departing from the boundaries of healthy, democratic debate."

And Mike Tapp, who was a Home Office minister under Keir Starmer, wrote: "Robert Jenrick should apologise for spreading misinformation about a Labour Minister. Fair and contentious debate is fine, spreading lies and misinformation is not."

‌



View 2 Images Mr Jenrick has come under fire over a post on X which he later deleted (Image: X)

In an interview with Talk TV's Jeremy Kyle, Mr Jenrick claimed he had been sent the clip by people who were at the meeting. He said: "I made the, I thought, perfectly reasonable point of putting that out into the public domain and asking her to explain what is her actual position. Now, she says that the recording isn't quite right, and that if you have a quality recording, she's saying something different.

2So, look, I am a fair minded person. I said late last night, you know what, I'll delete this. Let's give her the benefit of the doubt and let's see what she actually does."

Article continues below

Asked if he had made a mistake by putting it out, Mr Jenrick said: "No, I don't think so. But, look, I'm. I am prepared to give people the benefit of the doubt. I don't know exactly what happened at this meeting because I wasn't there."

However a Reform UK spokesman pointed the finger at news site Guido Fawkes, which it said was the source of the shorter quote shared by Mr Jenrick. He said: “We’ve always trusted Guido Fawkes as a source of information, but perhaps on this occasion they didn’t get the full picture.

"We await Burnham’s first mention of the small boats - he clearly doesn’t give a toss."

News.title: Firefighters face disciplinary probe after 'letting sick child ride fire engine'
News.content:
Firefighters face disciplinary probe after 'letting sick child ride fire engine'

A trio of firefighters from Greater Manchester could face serious disciplinary action after being reported for giving rides to small children during a community open day

View Image Firefighters could face serious disciplinary action over the incident (stock) (Image: Irish Daily Mirror)

A group of firefighters could face serious disciplinary action after they allegedly allowed a cancer-stricken young boy to have a ride on a fire engine.

‌



Three members of Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service are under investigation over the incident. They were reported after allegedly allowing a group of youngsters to briefly ride the fire engine during a community open day.

‌



The service believes the inquiry is justified as the rides took place on a public road, which could have potentially put the children in danger.

‌



An unnamed firefighter who spoke to Manchester Evening News on condition on anonymity said: "One of the children was a little boy who is recovering from cancer. It made both his day - and his parents'. The brigade is always pushing community engagement, then they react like this, which is completely over the top.

"It is a travesty. The engine went no more than a quarter of a mile down the road then circled a roundabout and came back. It was not even two minutes."

‌



He added: "The lad loves fire engines and it is the type of stuff done by many firefighters over the years. This is all part of a recent clampdown on discipline by the service's professional standards department. Really, in this case, a bit of common sense should have been applied.

"The case has infuriated the rank and file. They could be given a final written warning or worse and there is talk of possible industrial action - not striking - but some other action."

A Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service spokesperson said: "As a matter of policy, the Service does not comment on individual employee issues, investigations or disciplinary processes, whilst the matter is ongoing.

Article continues below

"Where concerns are raised regarding conduct, they are considered through the appropriate procedures to ensure the standards expected of Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service staff are maintained."

The source added: "It was an open day so the appliance would have been off the run and would only have been required if we had a huge fire which required multiple pumps."

News.title: Girl 'pulled from sea' on Torquay beach as coastguard scrambled
News.content:
Girl 'pulled from sea' on Torquay beach as coastguard scrambled

Emergency services rushed to Torre Abbey Beach after reports that a girl was in trouble in the water - she was treated by paramedics before being taken to hospital

View Image The incident happened at Torre Abbey Beach (stock image) (Image: GOOGLE MAPS)

A girl has been rushed to hospital after being "pulled from the water" after getting into difficulty in the sea in Torquay.

‌



Emergency services rushed to Torre Abbey Beach around 9.25pm on Wednesday night after reports that a girl was in trouble in the water.

‌



Multiple emergency vehicles attended the scene and the girl was treated by paramedics before being taken to hospital.

‌



One witness said: "Incident at Torquay seafront. Police, coastguard and ambulance on scene."

With the country having had its third heatwave in as many months, authorities have warned people of the dangers of entering open water. Tragically there have been dozens of deaths over the period.

The hazards from the hot weather have brought wildfires and several incidents where people have faced trouble in the water. Dave Swallow, National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) wildfire deputy lead and lead tactical adviser, warned of the dangers.

‌



British Airways flight makes emergency landing after fault discovered mid-air READ MORE :

He said: “Summer should be a time for people to enjoy the outdoors but it’s important not to underestimate the risks. Every year we see devastating wildfires and tragic drownings in inland water.

“As more schools break up for the summer holiday, we’re asking people to enjoy the warmer weather safely, look out for one another and take simple steps to help prevent avoidable tragedies.”

Among the deaths in recent weeks was an 18-year-old man whose body was recovered from the water near the weir at the Darley Abbey Mills complex after he and another teenager got into difficulty, said Derbyshire Constabulary.

‌



Greater Manchester Police said an 18-year-old male died at Dovestone Reservoir, Oldham, while two men died after going into the sea to try to help two children in Hartlepool.

Cleveland Police said officers were called at around 3.45pm on July 12 after concerns were raised for two children who had got into difficulty in the water at Seaton Carew beach in Hartlepool.

Two men entered the sea to assist the children, who were taken to hospital to be checked over and are now confirmed to be safe. RNLI staff brought the men out of the water and they received immediate medical treatment, but were pronounced dead a short time later.

Article continues below

Superintendent Glen Ward said: “I would like to remind everyone that open water comes with serious risks. We know it is inviting in the hot weather, but we would encourage people to refrain from entering any open water at all. Today we have sadly seen the true tragedy that can happen as a result. Please take extra care and enjoy the warm weather as safely as possible.”

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

That includes compulsory water safety lessons in schools, a nationwide public awareness campaign, better lifesaving equipment at high-risk waterways, the introduction of Sam's Law, and a dedicated Minister for Water Safety. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: Police officer was violent rapist who attacked women over 14 years, BBC reveals
News.content:
A police officer who took his own life in May was a violent rapist who carried out a spate of sexual attacks and attempted murders of women over at least 14 years, the BBC can reveal.

PC Alan Greer's first known victim was a woman he raped in her home in Glasgow in 2012 after she had called the police to report being the victim of a crime.

The woman reported the sex attack by Greer late last year, sparking one of Police Scotland's biggest ever anti-corruption inquiries.

Detectives have so far uncovered a further eight victims, five of whom were sex workers, attacked while Greer was off duty.

It has emerged that Greer used hundreds of prostitutes throughout his police career, and it is anticipated more victims of his violence will be identified.

Assistant Chief Constable Lynn Ratcliff, gold commander for the investigation, said what the inquiry had found was "truly shocking".

She said: "This officer has clearly abused his power and has revisited someone that he's encountered in the course of his duties.

"But this victim was brave enough to come and speak to us, and that really was the trigger point for us starting our investigation.

"That's allowed us to proactively identify eight further victims."

News.title: BBC visits Iran school where strike killed 120 children
News.content:
The school day had begun as usual, Amaineh says.

Because it was the Islamic holy month of Ramadan, the children gathered inside the prayer hall to recite the Quran, she recalls, before she began teaching her pupils a new letter of the Persian alphabet.

But, as the first attacks of the war unfolded across Iran, she says the headteacher announced the school would be closing, and teachers began contacting parents, urging them to collect their children.

Only five of Amaineh's 15 first-grade pupils were left in her classroom on the upper floor, she says, when she first heard an explosion not far from the school. She says she was in the corridor and rushed back for the children.

"Just as I went to leave, a missile struck the school," says Amaineh. "Something hit my head and my students' heads - we were all sent flying."

Then, she says, thick black smoke filled the classroom: "I couldn't even see the pupils I was holding in my arms. We couldn't breathe."

She says she remembers hearing another explosion, as well as the sounds of screaming, children crying and then the school itself collapsing â "destroyed all at once".

"Blood was pouring from me and the students," she adds.

News.title: Friend of Manchester synagogue attacker jailed for plot on military base
News.content:
A friend of the Manchester synagogue attacker has been jailed for life with a minimum of 17 years after the pair planned a separate attack on a military base.

Mohammad Bashir, 31, drove Jihad Al-Shamie on a 10-hour round trip to conduct hostile reconnaissance at the UK's Defence Academy in Shrivenham, Oxfordshire, on 14 August 2025.

Weeks after that journey, Al-Shamie, 35, was shot dead by police after carrying out the Heaton Park Synagogue attack, in which two Jewish men were killed.

Bashir was sentenced at Manchester Crown Court after pleading guilty to one count of preparing an act of terrorism.

Counter terror police uncovered Bashir's friendship with Al-Shamie after reviewing his phones following the attack on the synagogue in October 2025.

The pair held extremist views and had discussed preparing for "war" and frequently made antisemitic remarks in WhatsApp conversations, Greater Manchester Police said.

News.title: UK millionaires ask Andy Burnham to tax them more
News.content:
Millionaires including former footballer Gary Lineker and music producer Brian Eno have written to new prime minister Andy Burnham asking to be taxed more.

In an open letter, 120 well-off Britons told Burnham: "We can afford it. We're not talking about higher taxes on those who get up and go to work for their income every day, but on the very richest whose income is derived from the wealth they hold."

Organised by Patriotic Millionaires, the letter said it would lead to a more equal society, and urged a "devolution of wealth and power from the very richest".

People can already give money or stocks voluntarily to the Treasury using its donation facility.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Lineker is "very welcome to pay more tax he can write a cheque to the treasury, no one is stopping him."

The group supports a 2% tax on wealth over Â£10m.

"Millionaires are a patriotic bunch," the letter states. "We love this country and we want it to succeed.

"But success requires investment and a primary source of untouched capital investment is sitting with us, in untaxed potential."

Other signatories include Richard Curtis, director of Notting Hill and Love Actually and Ian Gregg, the former managing director of Greggs and son of the bakery chain's founder.

The renewed call for higher tax on the wealthy follows a similar campaign in previous years.

Burnham did not rule out a wealth tax when asked about it by Lineker a few days before he became prime minister.

He suggested he may have "to ask for a little more" tax at some point.

The latest call from Patriotic Millionaires said there is a "need to embrace a new kind of devolution of wealth and power, from the very richest in order to reinvest back into our greatest asset in every region".

It added that in its own poll, the majority of millionaires wanted a higher tax on themselves.

"There are a few people left with outdated economic thinking and few others desperate to hold onto every penny they can... Those that can't see past the end of their own self interest have no place in designing a Britain for the future," the letter said.

News.title: Airport drop-off fees up by a third - here are the priciest
News.content:
Drop-off fees at the UK's major airports have risen by a third on average since last summer, new analysis has found.

The RAC motoring group looked at the cost of pulling up to the closest point to terminals at the 20 busiest airports, 16 of which had put up their prices since last year.

London airport Gatwick topped the list by charging a "farewell fee" of Â£10 for 10 minutes. after lifting it by Â£3 from last year. Stansted also charges Â£10 but drivers are allowed 15 minutes at its "express set down" outside departures.

Airports UK, the trade body, said that free drop-offs were available and fees were part of airports' business models and climate change objectives.

The RAC said that the price of dropping people off in "kiss-and-fly" areas rose by an average of Â£1.70 to Â£7 compared to this time last year.

London City Airport, which only started making people pay this year, is the most expensive on a per-minute basis. Its Â£8 charge for five minutes works out at Â£1.60 per minute.

Birmingham is the cheapest, charging Â£7.00 for 15 minutes which equates to 47p per minute.

In contrast, none of the top 10 airports in the EU charge for drop-offs, according to RAC research.

News.title: Glasgow set to welcome the world for scaled back Commonwealth Games
News.content:
When the fastest man on the planet won Commonwealth relay gold for Jamaica in 2014, more than 50,000 fans cheered him home at Hampden.

But the athletes seeking to emulate Usain Bolt when the Games return to Glasgow - including mile world record holder Josh Kerr - will be competing at Scotstoun Stadium in front of 11,000 spectators.

This time round almost everything is on a smaller scale but organisers are confident fans will create a Tartan Army-style atmosphere for the 3,000 competitors who will be chasing glory.

From Friday until 2 August, 215 gold medals will be up for grabs - compared to 261 when Scotland last staged the Games - but Glasgow 2026 will see a record 47 para-sports events.

News.title: Rain to return this weekend as parts of UK on brink of drought
News.content:
If you cannot remember the last time it rained, you are probably not alone.

June was actually wetter than average in the UK, which might come as a surprise given our recent run of weather, but for England and Wales the majority of that rain came down in the first two weeks of the month.

Since 15 June, most of England has recorded less than 10mm of rain with large areas of central southern England seeing 3mm or less. Meanwhile, Wisley in Surrey has had no rain at all for 36 consecutive days.

Most of Wales has seen less than 25mm (1in) of rain since the middle of June, but it has been particularly dry in the north-east with Rhyl in Denbighshire recording only 3mm.

A Thames Water hosepipe ban came into force on Thursday, adding to other bans already in place for customers of other water companies across the south of the UK, as parts of southern, central and eastern England were declared to be close to drought.

Northern Ireland had a very wet June, recording 67% more rain than average, and it was also very wet in western Scotland. However, July has been much drier than average in Northern Ireland and most of Scotland, though the rain has continued in the Highlands, with Aultbea already reaching the July average rainfall, and with more on the way.

News.title: Why the UK is dithering over what to do about e-scooters
News.content:
When I step out of Southampton Central railway station, it takes me just seconds to spot an e-scooter. In this city, these devices have become a normal part of the transport ecosystem, along with e-bikes.

"It's just the most convenient way to commute from home to the station and back," says Keith Reed, who I speak to as he arrives at the station to catch a train to London. Keith says uses rental e-scooters twice a week. His alternative option would be his bike, but he'd then have to worry about where to leave it.

Around the city, there are parking areas for bright orange rental devices everywhere - but they're not necessarily a permanent feature. Southampton hosts one of the numerous government-backed trials around England. This one has been going on since 2021.

News.title: Life-changing MS drug to help people walk now on NHS in England
News.content:
The first drug to help people with multiple sclerosis walk is being made available on the NHS in England.

Fampridine boosts nerve signals to make it easier for some people to move and live independently.

Aysen Slack, who used to pay for fampridine privately until it became too costly, said the decision would make a "huge difference".

Up to 5,000 people in England could benefit each year. The drug is already available elsewhere in the UK.

Multiple sclerosis is caused by the immune system attacking the protective covering around nerve cells - known as myelin.

This damage impairs the ability of nerves to carry electrical messages from the brain to the rest of the body - including those needed for the precise control of muscles needed to walk.

Fampridine is known as a "signal booster" as it helps those electrical messages still get through.

Clinical trials showed around four in 10 people taking the drug had improvements in their walking speed and in how long they could walk for.

This could be the difference between getting around the house or needing help at home or enabling people to go out and see friends and family.

Current NHS support includes physiotherapy and walking aids.

The drug has previously been rejected for use by the NHS in England as it was not considered value for money, although it did become available in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

News.title: Former River City actor Iain Robertson jailed for nine years for rape
News.content:
The trial heard how Robertson, of Carbeth in Stirlingshire, raped a woman on one occasion between 2018 and 2019 as well as a separate sex assault.

The pair came to know each other from working together on River City.

The woman said she did not want anything sexual to happen, but believed Robertson did.

The relationship became intimate, but the woman later told Robertson she wanted their relationship to go back to being platonic.

She said one evening she was at his home in Glasgow's Tradeston and planned to sleep on the sofa, but Robertson allegedly told her she could join him in bed as "nothing would happen".

However, the witness said that the actor instead "had sex" with her.

She did not say anything to Robertson at the time, but said she did not participate in what happened and she did not want it to happen.

She also described an earlier incident when Robertson carried out a sex act on her and she "just waited for it to be over".

He was also found guilty of engaging in a course of abusive behaviour against her.

News.title: Animal lover run over by own car while saving cat on hill
News.content:
An animal lover was run over and killed by her own car after she got out to save a cat as the handbrake failed on a slope, an inquest has heard.

Jacqueline Davies, 75, climbed out of the driving seat of her red Ford Fiesta to move the cat to safety on 6 July while on a hill, but her car rolled forward and fatally struck her.

Gwent Coroner's Court heard Davies, from Hollybush in Cwmbran, Torfaen, was able to dial 999 after the incident, but died in hospital.

In a statement, Davies' family said she had a "strength that inspired those around her" and added they were "desperate for answers".

The inquest heard Davies was taken to University Hospital of Wales in Cardiff with serious injuries, and died the following day.

Coroner Rose Farmer said her provisional cause of death was given as a major haemorrhage, injury to the inferior vena cava - the largest vein in the body - and trauma.

Her family said: "We are heartbroken beyond words at the sudden loss of our beloved mum.

"She was a strong, independent, spirited mum who was never scared to speak her mind, and that was one of the many things we loved about her.

"She was honest, determined and full of character, with a strength that inspired those around her.

"Our family is devastated and life will never be the same without her.

"We are trying to come to terms with what has happened but we are also desperate for answers."

Gwent Police wants anyone travelling in the area of Bryn Millwr, Hollybush, on 6 July between 10:00 BST and 10:30 who may have witnessed the crash to contact officers.

The inquest into Davies' death will resume on 13 April 2027.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe public memorial to be held later this year, family says
News.content:
A public memorial for Ann Widdecombe will be held later this year, her family has said in a statement.

Former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman Widdecombe, 78, was found dead in her Dartmoor home with serious head injuries earlier this month.

Her family thanked the public for "the wide expression of condolences" but asked that her private service, to be held in the coming weeks and for which invitations have already been sent, is "limited to those closest to Ann".

"We understand that there is significant public interest in the funeral of Ann Widdecombe," the statement said.

"A private service for family and close friends will be held in the coming weeks, and invitations for this ceremony have been distributed.

"A more public memorial will follow later in the year, the details of which will be released in due course.

"While we are very grateful for the wide expression of condolences, the family would ask that this initial service is limited to those closest to Ann."

Tributes poured in to Widdecombe from TV stars and across the political spectrum following her death.

Anton Du Beke, who was her partner on Strictly Come Dancing in 2010, said he was devastated , which he called the "saddest of news".

"I had the most brilliant time with Ann on Strictly Come Dancing, she became a real friend, she was fun, she was upbeat, she was positive, she was supportive, she was game, wanted to enter into the spirit of the whole thing," he said in a video on X.

Kemi Badenoch, leader of the Conservative Party for which Widdecombe served as shadow home secretary from 1999 to 2001, said the party was "reeling".

She described Widdecombe as "a very fun and feisty woman who spoke her mind", while the then-Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer said Widdecombe was a "distinguished politician".

In a video posted on social media, Farage said Widdecombe was "an extraordinary woman" and "someone who gave her life to public service, to fighting for the things she believed in".

He described her as "a devout Christian and somebody with strong socially conservative views. Perhaps not popular in modern Britain but that is what Ann believed in".

News.title: Woman charged with man's retirement home murder
News.content:
A woman has been charged with murdering a 77-year-old man at a supported living retirement home.

Harry Heslop died after an incident at Cedar House in Foxwood Drive, Stockton, at about 02:45 BST on Tuesday, Cleveland Police said.

Rebecca Hackett, 41 and from Stockton, has been charged with murder and possession of a bladed article and is due to appear at Teesside Magistrates' Court later.

A second woman, aged 54, remains on bail while inquiries continue, the force said.

Det Ch Insp John Bonner said the force's thoughts were "firmly with Harry's family and loved ones at what is an extremely difficult and distressing time for them".

He thanked the local community for "their patience and support" and said police would be in the area to offer reassurance.

"As a criminal investigation is ongoing, we would ask people not to speculate as this may prejudice legal proceedings," Bonner said.

Housing association Thirteen Group, which runs Cedar House, previously said it was "deeply saddened" by the incident.

News.title: Secret court documents reveal potential scale of illegal sewage spilling
News.content:
Most of the sewage spills into England's waterways in the last two years may have been illegal but gone unpunished, according to new analysis.

UK law states that raw sewage should not be released during "normal" weather conditions, yet until now the regulator has not clarified exactly what that means.

But campaigner Prof Peter Hammond obtained a definition in secret court papers, and said it shows that for more than 80% of the time sewage was being spilled, the weather was "normal", making the spills possibly illegal.

The water companies and the regulator, the Environment Agency (EA), rejected the analysis and said they were working to reduce spill numbers.

News.title: Main ferry out of service for longer than planned
News.content:
The Isle of Man's main ferry will be out of action for longer than anticipated while "essential works" are carried out.

The island's ferry operator said "further necessary repairs" were needed after the Manxman entered drydock last week for scheduled maintenance.

The vessel has been replaced on the Douglas-Heysham route by former flagship ferry Ben-my-Chree, the Isle of Man Steam Packet Company said.

Back-up freight vessel MV Arrow is also set to return to the island while the Manxman is out of action. The operator said it was "reviewing its operational plans to minimise disruption" to passengers wherever possible.

The Ben-my-Chree had been due to take over as sole operator on the firm's Larne route from Friday.

That sailing will now be carried out by the fast craft Manannan.

News.title: Jet pioneer celebrated with new Royal Mail stamps
News.content:
The pioneering work on the jet engine by Sir Frank Whittle has been celebrated with a new set of stamps from Royal Mail.

Whittle, who was born in Coventry and founded Power Jets in Rugby to build the aircraft engines he designed, before going on to continue his pioneering work in Gloucestershire, died 30 years ago this year.

The stamps come in two sets, the first featuring four images of Whittle and his engines, while the second shows eight iconic British jet aircraft.

His son, Ian, said "It is a fitting tribute not only to my father's pioneering achievements, but also to the generations of engineers, designers and aviators who helped shape Britain's world-leading contribution to aviation."

Whittle was born in Coventry in 1907 and joined the RAF in 1923, training as an aircraft mechanic and graduating from RAF Cranwell as an officer in 1928.

Jason Sudeikis has spoken out about the alleged feud between himself and Ted Lasso showrunner Bill Lawrence, who left after season two.

Sudeikis, 50, is the star and co-creator of the football-themed Apple TV series, which returns for an unexpected fourth season next month following a three-year hiatus.

While several figures associated with the show claimed they witnessed mounting tension between the two, Sudeikis denied ever getting into any screaming matches with Lawrence in a new interview with The Hollywood Reporter.

open image in gallery Jason Sudeikis and Bill Lawrence pictured at the after-party for season two of ‘Ted Lasso’ in 2021 ( Getty )

“Bill never yelled at me and I never yelled at him,” said Sudeikis, who went on to say that he would have liked for Lawrence to stay on for the third season, which was, at the time, supposed to be the end.

“My preference would have been to land the plane with the same people we took off with.”

After Lawrence quit the show ahead of season three, he told The Hollywood Reporter: “It was healthy for me to let go the third year because Jason is Ted Lasso and, especially landing the plane, deserves it to be his vision – and I’ve reached a point in my career where I’m not the best at having to listen to other people over my own opinion.

Filming the third season without Lawrence proved difficult and costly, though, with star and co-creator Brendant Hunt describing it as “death by a thousand paper cuts”.

Showrunner Jack Burditt – behind sitcoms like 30 Rock and Modern Family – was tapped for the forthcoming fourth season, with Lawrence still involved only through his company Doozer Productions.

Burditt told The Hollywood Reporter that prior to him starting work on Ted Lasso’s fourth season, Lawrence called to give him “a lowdown of what to be prepared for”.

“He says, ‘Here’s how to deal with the show, here’s how to deal with Jason. …’ I think we spoke for about 20 minutes and then he said, ‘We should continue to have these conversations every one or two weeks,’ ” Burditt recalled, adding: “I have not talked to him since.”

On his working relationship with Sudeikis, Burditt said: “I know he’s got this reputation, and I know he drove Bill insane, but I honestly feel like Jason’s easy.”

open image in gallery Jason Sudeikis will return as Ted Lasso for season four of the Apple TV show ( Getty )

The fourth season of Ted Lasso will be released on 5 August, and will follow Sudeikis’s affable football coach as he embarks on a new chapter of his life, taking charge of a second-division women’s football team.

It is a switch-up from the previous three seasons, which saw Ted coach AFC Richmond’s men’s team – the cast of which had to be let go for this forthcoming season in a series of phone calls that Sudeikis described as “difficult”.

Hannah Waddingham, Brett Goldstein, and Juno Temple will reprise their roles in the forthcoming season.

Released in 2020, Ted Lasso has gone on to become a huge hit for Apple TV. The feel-good show won 13 Emmys and a Peabody award. Its success was hampered, however, by its third season, which was accused of losing its way, despite receiving positive reviews from critics.

Canelo Alvarez has suggested he will never box David Benavidez, saying “it’s not fair” that the Mexican-American fights in the weight classes he occupies.

Fans have long desired a showdown between Mexico’s Canelo, a former four-weight world champion, and Benavidez, a three-weight world champion, with many accusing Canelo of “ducking” the 29-year-old.

Canelo has held titles at super-welterweight, middleweight, super-middleweight, and even light-heavyweight, while Benavidez has held gold at super-middleweight, light-heavyweight and cruiserweight.

open image in gallery David Benavidez after stopping Gilberto 'Zurdo' Ramirez in May ( Getty )

Benavidez was even the WBC mandatory challenger to Canelo at super-middleweight for more than two years, without obtaining a fight with the 36-year-old. Benavidez thus moved up to light-heavyweight and, most recently, cruiserweight, where he took the WBA and WBO belts from Gilberto Ramirez with a stoppage win in May.

But Canelo has said he does not care about suggestions that he has avoided Benavidez, telling journalist Ariel Helwani: “I’m not worried because I did everything. I did everything in boxing. I accomplished everything in boxing, and I have nothing to prove, but yes, I will miss boxing a lot [when I retire].

“I’ve always been in that situation [of being called out], so it’s nothing strange for me. A lot of names out there, but when I beat them, then the other name comes. Right now, it’s Benavidez.

“He’s a heavyweight fighting in 175[lb], or cruiserweight, or something. But he’s a heavyweight. It’s not fair.

“When I turned undisputed [at super-middleweight for the second time], if he would be a champion at that point, that’s the correct time to do the fight. But he wasn’t, and he was fighting at 168[lb] at that point, but he wasn't a champion.”

Canelo also downplayed Benavidez’s status as a “Mexican” fighter, saying: “Not Mexican. It’s different, Mexican-American.”

Canelo was due to return against Christian Mbili in September, but that bout has been rescheduled for 31 October in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

open image in gallery Terence Crawford beat Canelo Alvarez (right) on points to become a three-weight undisputed champion ( Getty )

“I’m always very disciplined with my training, and I wasn’t ready to be in the training camp," Alvarez explained. “So, that’s why I postponed the fight, because I need to attend family first.

“All good now, I’m ready to train, and we are going to be [fighting] on 31 October.”

Canelo’s last bout was a points loss to Terence Crawford in September, as the American took the undisputed super-middleweight belts from the Mexican. With that result, Crawford stayed unbeaten and made history as boxing’s first three-weight undisputed champion in the four-belt era.

Crawford, 38, retired three months later, denying Canelo a rematch. Canelo underwent elbow surgery and is now preparing to challenge Mbili for the WBC super-middleweight title.
