World.title: Japan Tops Global Waste Index 2025; U.S., Israel, and Chile Rank as Worst Polluters
World.content:
Japan has emerged as the world leader in waste management, while Israel, Chile, and the United States rank among the worst-performing countries, according to the Global Waste Index 2025 released by Slovak-based waste technology company Sensoneo.

The report, which ranks all 38 OECD member states based on their waste generation and disposal practices, highlights significant disparities in global waste management. Sensoneoâs index evaluates countries on per capita waste generation, recycling, incineration, and landfill use.

Israel and Chile ranked last and second-to-last, respectively, primarily due to their heavy reliance on environmentally damaging landfilling practices. Israel sends 524 of the 650 kilograms of waste it generates per person each year directly to landfills. Chile recycles just 1% of its waste and sends more than 95% to landfill.

The United States, which increased its per capita waste generation from 811 to 951 kilograms since 2022, remains the highest generator of municipal solid waste globally. The U.S. disposes of nearly half of that â 447 kilograms â in landfills annually. Neighboring Canada also performed poorly, landfilling 67% of its annual 694 kg per capita waste.

At the other end of the spectrum, Japan ranked No. 1, followed by South Korea and Estonia, all of which combine relatively low waste generation with efficient disposal methods. Japan sends only 3 kilograms per capita to landfill, relying heavily on incineration (245 kg) and maintaining a controlled recycling rate.

European countries dominated the top 10 rankings, with Austria, Germany, Finland, Belgium, Sweden, Norway, and Switzerland all demonstrating strong waste management systems. Austria topped the recycling chart with 334 kilograms of municipal waste recycled per person annually â accounting for 42% of its total waste.

Meanwhile, Spain fell four places to 27th despite minor improvements. The country reduced its landfill and incineration rates slightly while increasing recycling by 10 kilograms per capita. However, its overall waste generation rose by 10 kg compared to the 2022 index.

The index revealed that in 12 of the 38 countries, over half of all waste is still landfilled â including in developed nations like Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By contrast, Switzerland was the only country to report zero landfill disposal, while Belgium, Finland, Estonia, and Japan landfilled less than 3 kg per person.

Other key findings include:

New Zealand , Finland , and Iceland posted the largest reductions in waste generation per capita.

, , and posted the largest reductions in waste generation per capita. From an environmental standpoint, incineration is considered preferable to landfilling, but excessive reliance on either suggests a need for stronger waste reduction and recycling strategies.

About the Index and Sensoneo

First launched in 2019, the Global Waste Index is published every three years by Sensoneo, a company specializing in digital transformation for waste management systems. The 2025 edition is based on the latest available national data.

Sensoneo operates in 87 countries and provides waste monitoring solutions to cities, industries, and governments. It is the only company to have successfully implemented deposit return systems (DRS) IT infrastructure in nine countries, achieving recycling rates above 90%.

In Madrid, Sensoneo is deploying 11,100 smart sensors, marking the worldâs largest smart waste monitoring installation to date.

World.title: South Korean Model and Actor Kim Jong Suk Dies at 29, Family Urges Respect Amid Speculation
World.content:
South Korean model and television personality Kim Jong Suk has died at the age of 29, his family confirmed on June 6. The news has shocked fans and colleagues across the countryâs entertainment industry, where Kim rose to prominence following his appearance on tvNâs 2022 reality dating show Skip Dating.

Kim, who began his career in modeling before transitioning to television, had been steadily gaining popularity in recent years. His sudden death has prompted an outpouring of grief and speculation online.

While the exact cause of death remains unconfirmed, some media reports have linked Kimâs passing to an incident in Hanam involving a violent altercation between a young man and his girlfriend. According to the reports, law enforcement responded to the scene, after which the man allegedly died by suicide after jumping from a high-rise building.

Amid widespread online discussion and conjecture, Kimâs family issued a public plea for restraint, asking the public and media to refrain from spreading misinformation or making disrespectful assumptions.

Kimâs older sister posted on social media, expressing the family’s devastation and emotional exhaustion. âWe ask for privacy and understanding during this difficult time,â she wrote, emphasizing the familyâs wish to grieve in peace.

Details regarding funeral arrangements have not been made public.

World.title: New York judge sets June 2027 for the start of Maduro and Cilia Flores's trial
World.content:
New York judge sets June 2027 for the start of Maduro and Cilia Flores's trial

23rd Thursday, July 2026 - 07:34 UTC Full article

Maduro, 63, is charged with conspiracy to commit narcoterrorism, cocaine importation, and possession of machine guns and destructive devices

Federal Judge Alvin Hellerstein set June 1, 2027, as the preliminary start date for the trial of former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, in the narcoterrorism case they face in the United States. The decision came on Wednesday during the case's third hearing before the US District Court for the Southern District of New York, which lasted only a few minutes.

Maduro, 63, is charged with conspiracy to commit narcoterrorism, cocaine importation, and possession of machine guns and destructive devices. Flores, 69, faces charges linked to drug importation and weapons possession. Both have pleaded not guilty to all counts and have been held at a federal prison in Brooklyn since January 3, when they were captured in Caracas during a US military operation.

The schedule, jointly proposed by prosecutors and the defense the previous day, contemplates two rounds of pretrial motions. The defense will file a first set before September 2 arguing Maduro's immunity as the head of a sovereign state, one of its central contentions. According to his lawyer, Barry Pollack, if that motion succeeds, the second round would not be necessary. Prosecutors expect to complete the handover of unclassified evidence by September 22 and of classified material by November 15. Hellerstein called a hearing for November 17 to debate those arguments.

“This is a realistic schedule, we don't think it will be delayed,” Pollack said, after the judge voiced doubts about the parties' ability to meet the deadlines set for submitting evidence, witnesses, and experts.

Demonstrators for and against the proceedings gathered near the courthouse, with police present to prevent incidents, as had happened at the March hearing. From Caracas, the former president's son and lawmaker for the governing PSUV, Nicolás Maduro Guerra, called the process “unjust” and demanded his parents' release.

The case earlier saw a dispute over funding for the defense: Maduro and Flores argued they could not pay private lawyers because of US sanctions and because they were barred from using Venezuelan state funds. In April, Washington authorized Venezuela to cover their legal representation.

Since the capture, Venezuela has been governed by former vice-president Delcy Rodríguez, under whose tenure the United States eased sanctions on the oil industry. The former president also faces other civil proceedings in the United States: last week, a Miami judge issued a default judgment ordering him, along with other officials, to pay $314 million to three US citizens.

World.title: Wes Streeting appointed UK Defence Secretary; ‘disappointment’ with removal of Dan Jarvis, responsible for DIP
World.content:
Wes Streeting appointed UK Defence Secretary; ‘disappointment’ with removal of Dan Jarvis, responsible for DIP

23rd Thursday, July 2026 - 07:34 UTC Full article

“With John Healey now looking after the money, Wes Streeting can focus on the vital Defence Reforms necessary to deliver.”

Former Health and Social Care Secretary Wes Streeting has been appointed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham as the new UK Defense Secretary, replacing Dan Jarvis who has taken the job when John Healey resigned last June.

This means Jarvis was Defence Secretary for less than six weeks – but in that time he was responsible for publishing the long awaited Defense Investment Plan (DIP), and there was expectation across the forces whether PM Burnham would keep his in Defense..

However taking to social media after it was announced that Streeting would replace him in the role, Mr Jarvis said: “It’s been an immense honor to serve as Defense Secretary and again be amongst those who give everything to defend our nation.”

“We owe them a huge debt of gratitude — and they will always have my absolute support. I wish my successor every success in this vital role.”

Former conservative Defence Secretary Ben Wallace criticized Mr Burnham’s decision to replace Mr Jarvis .

“Removing Dan Jarvis to find a spot for Wes Streeting shows a contempt for Defense at a time they need continuity and someone who understands the new way of warfare and the men and women of the armed forces,” he posted on X.

But there was a more positive reaction to the news from retired Air Marshal Greg Bagwell, a former combat pilot and senior leader in the RAF, who said: “With John Healey now looking after the money, Wes Streeting can focus on the vital Defense Reforms necessary to deliver.”

Meanwhile, a former head of the British Army has also said he is “disappointed” that Wes Streeting has been made defense secretary but spoke more positively about the potential relationship between Mr Streeting and his predecessor in the Treasury.

Lord Dannatt told Times Radio: “A new defense secretary has a lot to learn – the defense portfolio is one of the more complicated ones in government and as far as I’m aware Wes Streeting has got no background in defense, no background in the military”. (Forces)

World.title: Stephen Doughty confirmed as Minister of State for Overseas Territories
World.content:
Stephen Doughty confirmed as Minister of State for Overseas Territories

23rd Thursday, July 2026 - 02:00 UTC Full article

Minister Doughty during a meeting in London with MLA Roger Spink

Stephen Doughty MP has been confirmed at Minister of State in the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office. Until 21 July 2026 and from 8 July 2024 he was previously Minister of State for Europe, North America and Overseas Territories in the FCDO.

Stephen was first elected as Welsh Labour and Co-operative Member of Parliament for Cardiff South and Penarth in November 2012.

Stephen studied at Lester B. Pearson UWC in Canada, Oxford University and St Andrews University. He later worked for the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly and for members of the then National Assembly for Wales.

Stephen spent a number of years working for humanitarian and international development NGOs World Vision UK, Oxfam GB, Oxfam International and Oxfam Cymru. During the previous Labour government he was Special Adviser to the Secretary of State for International Development.

Stephen served at the Wales, Home Affairs, Arms Export Controls and International Development Committees in Parliament. He was also an opposition Whip and a Shadow Minister for Trade and Industry. He chaired the All-Party Parliamentary Group for HIV and Aids, and was a member of the British-Irish Parliamentary Assembly.

Stephen completed the Armed Forces Parliamentary scheme, attending the Royal College of Defense Studies 2017 to 2018. He has also served as an Army Reservist. In 2020 he was appointed Shadow Foreign Affairs and International Development Minister and in 2021 he was appointed Shadow Minister for Europe, North America and the Overseas Territories.

Stephen Doughty as Minister for Europe last week signed the UK/EU treaty on Gibraltar, ensuring ministerial continuity at the FCDO. Gibraltar media reported his reappointment is significant in the implementation phase of the treaty and when the treaty comes to be ratified by the House of Commons under the process set out in the Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010.

As a UK Government minister, Mr Doughty was closely involved in the final phases of the negotiation on the treaty and has close knowledge of the matter. He is also well versed in Gibraltar issues, having visited the Rock on numerous occasions in recent years including for National Day celebrations.

“I’m delighted to see that Stephen has been reappointed to the post of Minister for Europe,” said Chief Minister Fabian Picardo, reacting to the news. “He has a deep knowledge of the issues affecting Gibraltar from his time in Opposition and in Government.”

World.title: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, no friend of “Trumpism”, White House
World.content:
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, no friend of “Trumpism”, White House

23rd Thursday, July 2026 - 01:57 UTC Full article

Miliband’s political positions have frequently put him at odds with the White House: he led opposition within the National Security Council to the use of UK bases for US bombers

Reports from the United States indicate the White House has raised concerns about UK Premier Andy Burnham’s decision to appoint Ed Miliband as foreign secretary, amid warnings from the Donald Trump administration that he could create tensions in the UK-US relationship, according to reports Tuesday.

One senior US official reportedly told the Telegraph that Miliband would be a “point of friction” because of his support for green energy policies that Trump has criticized.

The warning is understood to have been made during unofficial “access” talks between the Trump administration and Burnham’s team after it became clear that Burnham was the leading candidate to replace Keir Starmer.

Miliband’s political positions have frequently put him at odds with the White House. In February, he led opposition within the National Security Council to the use of UK bases for US bombers, a dispute that contributed to a deterioration in Starmer’s relationship with the president, who described the prime minister as “not Winston Churchill.”

The opposition resulted in Starmer denying a US request to use Diego Garcia, the strategically significant military base in the Chagos Islands, at the beginning of the US’ and Israel’s war on Iran.

Miliband has also faced criticism from Trump allies for his approach to energy policy. As energy secretary, he blocked new licenses for oil and gas drilling in the North Sea, a move at odds with Trump’s support for increased domestic fossil fuel production.

The foreign secretary’s previous comments about Trump have also come under scrutiny. In 2016, Miliband wrote, “We must do our best at home and abroad to resist the worst of Trumpism … These are dark days for America and the world. There can be little solace right now.”

In 2017, Miliband said Trump had “lowered the bar for idiocy” and later joined a Stop Trump March in London.

World.title: Report says Trump is pushing Infantino to lead the UN
World.content:
Report says Trump is pushing Infantino to lead the UN

22nd Wednesday, July 2026 - 22:26 UTC Full article

According to those sources, Trump believes the football official, 56, who holds dual Swiss and Italian nationality, is “respected by everyone around the world”

US President Donald Trump is promoting FIFA President Gianni Infantino as a candidate to succeed António Guterres at the head of the United Nations, according to the New York Post, which cited anonymous sources close to the White House. The information has not been officially confirmed by the US government or FIFA, and Infantino himself has not commented publicly.

According to those sources, Trump believes the football official, 56, who holds dual Swiss and Italian nationality, is “respected by everyone around the world” and has “a special ability to bring people together.” The president's special envoy for global partnerships, Paolo Zampolli, endorsed the idea in remarks to the same newspaper, the only openly stated backing so far.

Any such candidacy would face procedural and political hurdles. The next secretary-general must first secure a recommendation from the Security Council, where the United States holds veto power, before being confirmed by the General Assembly. Guterres leaves office on December 31, at the end of his second term.

The proposal would also upend an established expectation in multilateral diplomacy. Under the informal regional rotation norm governing the appointment, the next secretary-general had been expected to come from Latin America and the Caribbean. Names in circulation include former Chilean president Michelle Bachelet, Mexico's Alicia Bárcena, Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan, Ecuador's María Fernanda Espinosa, and Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley, as well as Argentina's Rafael Grossi, director of the International Atomic Energy Agency.

Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, has already announced his intention to seek a third term at the organization. His relationship with Trump grew closer during the 2026 World Cup, hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada. FIFA opened an office in Trump Tower in New York, and Infantino presented the president with the first Peace Prize created by the body, last December. The two appeared together at Sunday's final award ceremony, when they handed the trophy to Spain.

That proximity drew controversy during the tournament. Trump called Infantino to request a review of the red card given to US forward Folarin Balogun, after which FIFA's disciplinary committee suspended the ban, an unprecedented decision that drew criticism from UEFA and other federations.

Across his two terms, Trump has maintained a tense relationship with the United Nations and has questioned the role of multilateral bodies, in addition to withdrawing the United States from the Paris Agreement and the World Health Organization.

World.title: A young Falkland Islander will represent the islands at the Commonwealth Youth Parliament in Sydney
World.content:
A young Falkland Islander will represent the islands at the Commonwealth Youth Parliament in Sydney

22nd Wednesday, July 2026 - 22:13 UTC Full article

Lee is a Falkland Islands student currently studying veterinary nursing in the United Kingdom and serves as a junior ambassador for the islands (Pic FB)

The Falkland Islands Legislative Assembly announced that Jessica Lee will represent the territory at the Commonwealth Youth Parliament, to be held from July 26 to 31 in Sydney, hosted by the Parliament of New South Wales, Australia.

Lee is a Falkland Islands student currently studying veterinary nursing in the United Kingdom and serves as a junior ambassador for the islands. According to the official statement, she brings to the role first-hand experience of life in Camp — as the rural area outside Stanley is known locally — as well as of farming, tourism, and conservation work. She has previously represented the islands in engagements with the Speaker of the British House of Commons and took part in an exchange of correspondence with schools in Argentina. In 2025 she was named Apprentice of the Year.

During the week of activities, the delegate will join representatives from across the Commonwealth in a full programme within the New South Wales Parliament, including caucus sessions, committee debate, and a whole-house sitting on a bill concerning artificial intelligence and democratic integrity. The agenda also includes cultural and diplomatic engagements, among them a reception at the British Consulate-General in Sydney.

“Jessica representing the Falklands in Sydney is the kind of opportunity we are proud that young Falkland Islanders have,” said Member of the Legislative Assembly Stacy Bragger, portfolio holder for Education and Community. He added that this kind of international representation sends, in his view, “a strong message” overseas about what he described as the everyday reality of self-determination in the islands' community.

The delegate herself expressed enthusiasm for the experience. “I am really looking forward to meeting my other Youth Parliament members and getting to represent my home on the global stage,” she said, adding that she is interested in politics and hopes to learn about other countries' cultures and stories.

The Commonwealth Youth Parliament is an annual activity that brings together young delegates from the organization's countries and territories to simulate the workings of a parliament, with debates on bills and legislative procedure.

The Falklands, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic, take part in various Commonwealth activities. The archipelago is the subject of a sovereignty dispute between the United Kingdom and Argentina, which claims the islands and maintains that the question should be settled through bilateral negotiations. This is the second public statement the Assembly has issued this week, following its congratulations to the new British prime minister, Andy Burnham.

World.title: US court upholds $390 million judgment against Argentina over Aerolíneas
World.content:
US court upholds $390 million judgment against Argentina over Aerolíneas

22nd Wednesday, July 2026 - 22:13 UTC Full article

The decisive legal point was the statute of limitations

The US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit on Tuesday rejected an appeal filed by Argentina and left standing the ruling that recognizes an arbitral award of $390,907,115 in favor of the fund Titan Consortium, over the 2008 expropriation of Aerolíneas Argentinas and Austral Líneas Aéreas Cielos del Sur. The amount was calculated as of December 10, 2024, with subsequent interest to be added.

The ruling does not require immediate payment, but strengthens the fund's position in the enforcement process, allowing it to continue legal proceedings in the United States in search of Argentine assets against which to collect.

The decisive legal point was the statute of limitations. Argentina argued that a three-year period should apply, while the District Court had ruled in 2024 that the applicable period was twelve years. The appeals court upheld that reasoning and dismissed the country's request to throw out the claim.

The litigation dates back to the expropriation ordered under the government of Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, when the airlines were controlled by Spain's Marsans group. In July 2017, an arbitral tribunal of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID), part of the World Bank, ordered Argentina to pay some $321 million plus interest and costs. The country sought to annul that award, which became final in 2019.

The economic rights to the claim changed hands in the litigation-finance market. After the award, they passed to Britain's Burford Capital — the same firm behind the lawsuit over the renationalization of YPF — which in 2018 sold them to Titan Consortium for about $107 million. Because ICSID awards are not automatically enforceable, Titan petitioned US courts in 2021 for recognition of the award in order to pursue assets.

According to analyst Sebastián Maril, director of Latam Advisors, the decision also revives the Webuild case, which had been on hold pending this outcome.

Argentina's Treasury Attorney General's Office, responsible for the state's legal defense, said it is analyzing “all available legal tools to overturn or at least mitigate the impact of that ruling.” The agency attributed the origin of the case to decisions taken nearly two decades ago and to what it described as an inheritance of lost lawsuits, an assessment reflecting the current government's position on litigation begun under previous administrations.

The case adds to the series of proceedings Argentina faces in foreign courts over past expropriations and economic decisions, with potential implications for its assets abroad.

World.title: Burnham’s Britain: what kind of country has UK’s new prime minister inherited?
World.content:
Burnham’s Britain: what kind of country has UK’s new prime minister inherited?

22nd Wednesday, July 2026 - 09:26 UTC Full article

UK will have its seventh prime minister in the ten years since it voted to leave EU. It begs the question: what is it about the UK that makes governing it so difficult at this point in time?

By Ben Wellings, Associate Professor in Politics and International Relations, Monash University - When Andy Burnham was handed the keys to 10 Downing Street on Monday, the United Kingdom will have its seventh prime minister in the ten years since it voted to leave the European Union. It begs the question: what is it about the UK that makes governing it so difficult at this point in time?

At the risk of sounding like a broken record, a large part of the answer is Brexit. But Brexit only expressed and exacerbated some of the structural problems the UK still faces today: cynicism, pessimism and political polarization; uncertain relations with the rest of the world; declining living standards for the poorest in society; a sense of social fragmentation; poorly maintained public services… and England knocked out of the World Cup in the semi-finals.

The last point is not trivial, at least in as much as it draws attention to the structure of the UK. The political elephant in the room is England. Specifically, it is the politics of nationhood in England that Burnham needs to address if Labour is to retain office whenever the next election is called.

England needs practical policies to address social and regional inequalities. Importantly, these policies must support a renewed national narrative that explains England’s place in the UK, and the UK’s place in Europe and the world.

Lest this should be seen as a trivial endeavour, it’s worth remembering that Keir Starmer’s lack of a positive narrative meant his political honeymoon with the electorate was very short.

Furthermore, national narratives need to have some grounding in reality. Boris Johnson’s hyperbolic narratives served as an example of how excessive claims – in this case of restored greatness – can erode trust and increase a sense of distance between the audience and the author of such claims.

Establishing a positive national narrative is no easy task. First, it will have to address some inherent contradictions. England is a diverse but singular entity. Through the UK, it has a relationship with the EU built on a newfound – and for many unwanted – sovereignty. It is a nation that values fairness but is increasingly unequal. And that’s before we get to the fact that the contemporary media environment favors, and at times actively supports, a sense of nationhood based on anger and grievance.

Burnham has a partial answer to the English question: the devolution of decision-making powers to local communities. This is a variation on the “take back control” theme – this time from Westminster rather than the EU.

Whereas Starmer was identified as being from southern England (despite being born in Yorkshire) because he supported Arsenal and had “Sir” in front of his name, Burnham wears his northern Englishness on his sleeve. His “Manchesterism” draws on the cooperative traditions of that part of England and inclines him towards greater state intervention in the economy – which will no doubt be resisted in some bastions of London’s financial district, and by tech giants.

So when some people talk about Burnham as the “king of the North”, or when he says he will establish a “Number 10 North” to bring policy focus to places like his Greater Manchester constituency of Makerfield, the “north” we are talking about is not Scotland. It is implicitly the north of England. This is where the next election will be won and lost as Labour confronts the radical right insurgent party Reform UK.

As in Australia with support from One Nation, there is a deep well of pessimism, anger and anxiety that has been exacerbated by the post-pandemic pressure on living costs. In the UK, these pressures compounded existing hardships caused by the imposition of austerity measures and the slow, deflating effects of Brexit on the UK economy.

But this politics of pessimism plays out in the UK’s peculiar structure. It’s worth remembering how unusual the UK is as a nation-state – if indeed we can use that term to describe it. It is comprised of (at least) four different nations. It is not a federation, but an asymmetrically devolved union that retains atypical levels of centralized governmental control.

What used to be an electorate fairly evenly divided between the Conservatives and Labour has now become fragmented between seven different parties across its many devolved jurisdictions with different voting systems. In Scotland and Wales, notionally secessionist parties govern. The government of Northern Ireland is led by a party that claims it wants to reunite Ireland. In England, British nativism is mobilized by the radical and far-right.

It is in this difficult context that Burnham needs to find a narrative for his government that links government policies with “Labour values” and speaks directly to England as a political community. Labour governments tend to be short, but with long-lasting impacts. This suggests a bold policy agenda rather than Starmer-like managerialism. Plans to re-nationalize failing privatized water utilities would be a good place to get some early runs on the board and signal that market-based solutions have their limitations.

As English football fans know, it’s the hope that kills you. Hope among Labour supporters is again high, but it may be the UK’s structural problems run too deep for a change of manager to alter their course. This may make Burnham’s main political task – defeating Reform with its transnational crypto currency financial support – harder.

At least over the summer Burnham and Labour can enjoy the political farce of Nigel Farage scoring an own goal in a self-called by-election in his seaside constituency of Clacton.

Farage resigned as MP for Clacton to defer parliamentary judgement on huge crypto donations from outside the UK. All other parties sensed the trap and declined to field candidates, leaving novelty candidate Count Binface as Farage’s sole challenger. A Binface victory would be a win for the ages.

No one said the English don’t have a sense of humor. (The Conversation)

World.title: Mexico is attracting more tourists — but they’re spending less
World.content:
Although Mexico continues to receive a growing number of international visitors, tourists are spending less during their stay.

Confirming the higher volume-lower value trend, the consulting firm Gemes Consultores reported that international tourist arrivals increased by 5.3% between January and May compared with the same period of 2025, but tourism revenue fell 0.4% as average spending per visitor fell 4.9%.

The firm cautioned that Mexico is increasingly becoming a mass tourism destination, rather than one focused on higher-spending visitors.

Another data source, the International Travelers Survey (EVI) conducted by the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI), broadly reflects the same trend. Mexico received 8.36 million international travelers in May, but total visitor spending fell 0.6%, while average spending per tourist slipped 4.9%, from US $626 to US $596.

“We are receiving a relatively larger number of low-spending tourists and, in relative terms, fewer high-spending tourists,” Gemes Consultores told news outlet Imagen Radio.

Gemes Consultores attributed the change to the increase in border tourism which has taken ground away from air arrivals.

Air tourism — the highest spending sector at US $1,310.70 per person — accounted for 47.9% of visitors between January and May, down 58.1% compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, border tourism — which spends significantly less at US $117 — increased its share from 39.5% to 44.8%.

In May alone, international air arrivals declined by 9.0%, driven largely by a U.S. market contraction of 12.4%, which Gemes identifies as the main driver behind the decline.

“This contraction is the primary factor explaining the overall performance of air arrivals during the first five months, with a 4.5% drop,” the company said.

This downward trend aligns with other recent indicators in the sector. Tourist hotspots like Los Cabos, Cancún, and Puerto Vallarta are facing a decline in high-spending tourism, amid reduced air connectivity, shifts in travel preferences, and increased competition from destinations in Europe and Asia.

The decline in international air arrivals has also generated concerns among airlines and industry analysts, since travelers arriving by air typically spend more than border visitors.

“It is urgent to reverse this situation and implement effective strategies to reactivate the arrival of tourists by air,” Gemes Consultores concluded.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Morena rolls out anti-corruption screening for 2027 candidates
World.content:
Morena, Mexico’s ruling party, will use a “double filter” to ensure that its candidates in the 2027 elections have no criminal links and have not committed any other offenses.

Morena President Ariadna Montiel announced the measure at a press conference on Tuesday, explaining that one check on potential candidates will be conducted by the party itself while another is set to be carried out by the federal government’s Security Cabinet, if it agrees to do so.

Montiel said that everyone vying to represent Morena at federal, state and municipal elections in 2027 will have to pass both checks in order to be ratified as candidates. That includes people seeking the office of governor, federal deputy, state deputy, mayor and other municipal positions, she said.

“Each and everyone” will have to pass the filters, Montiel said.

“We’re talking about just over 20,000 primary and substitute candidates,” she said.

The two checks, or filters, will seek to detect any criminal links potential candidates may have as well as determine whether they have committed any crimes, such as violence against women.

Montiel said that people selected as candidates by Morena will also be subjected to criminal checks undertaken by the National Electoral Institute (INE). For Morena candidates, that check will serve as a third filter. The Federal Attorney General’s Office and the Finance Ministry’s Financial Intelligence Unit will assist the INE in its review process. All political parties have the option of asking the INE to conduct checks on their potential candidates, in addition to carrying out their own internal processes.

Morena’s decision to use a double filter to assess the propriety of political aspirants comes almost three months after the unsealing of an indictment in which U.S. prosecutors accuse several Morena party politicians, including Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and Senator Enrique Inzunza, of drug trafficking in league with the Sinaloa Cartel.

How will Morena’s ‘double filter’ work?

Montiel said that Morena will first use “open sources” to check whether potential candidates have engaged in criminal conduct or any other unbecoming behavior including “frivolities” that are incongruent with the party’s “principles.”

Those open sources include social media accounts of potential candidates.

“In open sources you can have access to … a good part of all of our lives,” Montiel said.

Morena officials will also examine letters that land on the desk of Montiel, who became national leader of the party founded by ex-president Andrés Manuel López Obrador in May.

“People send me little letters and one finds out about things that one probably wouldn’t find out about otherwise,” the Morena president said.

Regarding the second filter, Montiel said that Morena would ask the Security Cabinet, a group of top federal security officials, to “support us with the review.”

She said that review would be conducted “within the framework” of the Security Cabinet’s “powers” and in accordance with the law.

Montiel noted that there is an online “platform” with information on “everyone” who has been arrested and convicted of committing a crime.

She said that potential Morena candidates “already know” that their past and present conduct will be thoroughly examined. Any political aspirants considered unsuitable “won’t be candidates,” Montiel said.

If someone has done “improper things, he or she won’t be allowed to contest an election as a Morena candidate, she said.

Morena — which is Mexico’s dominant political party, governing at the federal level and in 23 of the 32 federal entities — and the federal Security Cabinet will have to carry out their checks of political aspirants relatively quickly as the formal “electoral process” for the June 2027 elections will commence in September.

With reports from Animal Político, El Heraldo de México and Milenio

World.title: Guelaguetza, Oaxaca’s world renowned ethnic festival, gets underway
World.content:
A packed house of more than 11,000 people was on hand Monday for the opening of the 94th edition of Oaxaca’s famous Guelaguetza festival.

The first Monday on the Hill kicked off what is widely considered Latin America’s largest ethnic celebration, with 13 delegations from across the state presenting dances, music and regional customs.

The festivities took place in the Guelaguetza Auditorium, an open-air amphitheater built in the 1970s on the slope of Cerro del Fortín above Oaxaca’s historic center.

Modernized and renovated from 2008 to 2010, the facility will also host a second Lunes del Cerro (Monday on the Hill) on July 27 — part of the closing stretch of the festival, even as side fairs and events continue.

As in 2025 and years past, the opening show focused on the traditions and music of Oaxaca’s 16 Indigenous peoples and Afro-Mexican communities.

Enid Azucena Torres Agustiniano — a nursing student, cyclist and activist for Afro-Mexican rights — was chosen by the state’s Ministry of Culture and Arts as the festival’s official ambassador, Goddess Centéotl.

The first Afro-Mexican woman to serve in that role, Torres is originally from Santiago Pinotepa Nacional in the Costa Chica area, a corridor on the coast of Oaxaca and Guerrero with some of Mexico’s highest concentrations of Afro-Mexican communities.

“Being Afro-Mexican is not something to hide,” Torres told the audience. “It is something to honor and live with dignity.”

Opening day featured performances from communities including Ciudad Ixtepec, San Juan Bautista Tuxtepec and Santiago Pinotepa Nacional. Signature moments included a sing-along of “Dios Nunca Muere” and closing dances that drew standing ovations.

“Oaxaca is a melting pot of our country’s cultures,” Federal Tourism Minister Josefina Rodríguez Zamora said in a press release. “Here, our history, our traditions and the pride of our people come alive.”

The festival traces its roots to a Zapotec ritual known as Daninayaaloani, or Hill of the Beautiful View, in honor of Centéotl, the corn goddess. As part of that ritual, people gathered over eight days to share offerings, eat and dance.

In the Zapotec language, “Guelaguetza” refers to reciprocal offerings — a tradition of giving and sharing within the community.

Officials said the current festivities, running throughout the month of July, include more than 140 events statewide, from fairs and parades to gastronomic and artisanal exhibitions.

Tourism officials said they expect about 149,000 visitors, an economic impact exceeding 668 million pesos (US $38.4 million) and average hotel occupancy of 83%.

With reports from Infobae, El Universal Oaxaca, Político MX and Reporte Indig

World.title: Guadalajara residents receiving contaminated water will get an 80% discount on their bills
World.content:
Guadalajara households are eligible for an 80% discount on their water bills once they’re verified as having been affected by the contaminated water problem plaguing the state capital.

The discount, approved Monday by the Jalisco state Congress, will apply until December 15 to approximately 600 neighborhoods and as many as 750,000 beneficiaries supplied by the Intermunicipal System of Potable Water and Sewerage Services (SIAPA).

Congress will consult with the state Human Rights Commission to determine which neighborhoods have been affected, according to the president of the Finance Commission, Congresswoman Gabriela Cárdenas Rodríguez.

The Human Rights Commission will report the neighborhoods from which it has received complaints during 2026, with areas being added to the list throughout the year upon their request and with the approval of the SIAPA governing board.

The decision came after Guadalajara Morena party Councilman José María Martínez delivered a citizen petition to the local Congress on July 13, signed by 31,508 people and titled “If there is no clean water, no payment.” The measure aimed to support families who have not been provided with the water quality and hygiene standards they are entitled to by law.

The discount has been set at 80% because the remaining 20% of the user fee to SIAPA contributes to the operation of non-water services, such as drainage, sewage and other sanitary infrastructure.

To receive the discount, users must meet the following conditions:

Live in a neighborhood included in the list of affected areas.

Have been receiving poor-quality or cloudy water.

Have a monthly consumption of up to 25 cubic meters.

Be a residential or small business user.

Not belong to the industrial sector or be a large consumer.

During the same session, the Finance Committee approved another initiative to eliminate 100% of the late fees generated by outstanding water bills.

Also, Jalisco Governor Pablo Lemus Navarro has outlined an investment of 100 million pesos (US $5.7 million) for the use of portable water treatment plants, which will rotate across different areas of the city to provide clean drinking water to affected neighborhoods.

With reports from La Jornada, N+ Noticias and Eje Central

World.title: El Jalapeño: Hummingbirds lead a very ‘unhealthy’ lifestyle, says Mexico’s Health Ministry
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. This one was sent in by a reader.

In an unprecedented public advisory released Tuesday, Mexico’s Health Ministry condemned what it called “a reckless, sugar-fueled epidemic sweeping backyards, gardens and hanging feeders nationwide.” In other words, the hummingbird’s diet. This diet, officials said, places the birds at risk for what authors describe as “a lifetime of poor nutritional choices.”

When informed that hummingbirds have evolved over 42 million years to metabolize nectar at extraordinary rates, Dr. Elena Paloma, chair of the advisory panel, responded, “That’s exactly the kind of outdated thinking we’ve been trying to overcome.”

The 312-page report, “Hummingbirds: The Hidden Dangers of Nectar Dependency,” states that hummingbirds derive nearly 99% of their daily calories from sugar water and flower nectar while consuming “woefully inadequate amounts of kale, quinoa and lean poultry.”

“We’re done pretending this is ‘nature’ and not a public health emergency,” the report states.

The report also notes, with alarm, that a hummingbird’s heart can beat up to 1,200 times per minute. The Health Ministry attributes this not to one of the most extraordinary metabolic adaptations in the animal kingdom, but to “an all-carb diet finally catching up to them.”

Environmental groups expressed concern that the report unfairly stigmatizes hummingbirds. “They flap their wings up to 80 times a second,” said one ornithologist. “By lunchtime, they’ve burned enough calories to power a small drone.”

The advisory acknowledges this but notes that “exercise alone cannot compensate for poor dietary habits,” citing studies of office workers who occasionally use the stairs. Recommended interventions include: mandatory nutrition labels on nectar listing “added sugars” in bold red letters; a national campaign urging Mexicans to fill feeders with a “more balanced” ratio of sugar water, electrolytes and vitamins; and warning labels on flowers reading, “This bloom may contribute to excessive wing-flapping.”

Early field trials have yielded mixed results. “We filled our feeder with cucumber-infused electrolyte water,” said one volunteer. “The hummingbirds looked at it for about three seconds and then flew across the street to our neighbor’s house.”

Several violet-crowned hummingbirds observed near a patch of trumpet vine declined to comment, choosing instead to hover silently before accelerating from 0 to 30 miles per hour in approximately half a heartbeat.

Manufacturers of hummingbird feeders have pledged to cooperate by adding warning labels:

“Warning: Frequent consumption of sugar water may contribute to rapid wing movement, hyperactivity and an irresistible attraction to brightly colored tubular flowers.”

The Health Ministry said its next report will examine the dependence of monarch butterflies on milkweed, ocelots on tropical rodents and jaguars on peccaries, warning that “dietary diversity is essential, even when evolution strongly suggests otherwise.”

World.title: Greer joins USMCA talks in Mexico City to push for stronger automotive rules of origin
World.content:
The U.S. government, which announced on July 1 that it had declined to renew the United States-Mexico-Canada-Agreement (USMCA) in its current form, is seeking stronger automotive sector rules of origin (ROOs) in the North American free trade pact.

In a report submitted to U.S. Congress this month, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that his office, the USTR, “intends to examine carefully the USMCA’s automotive rules of origin to identify areas where stronger rules can directly benefit U.S. manufacturers and workers.”

In the foreword of the same report — titled “Report to Congress on the Operation of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement with respect to Trade in Automotive Goods” — Greer said that “the automotive industry remains a significant contributor to the U.S. and North American economies” and “the USMCA has had a positive impact on the global competitiveness of the regional auto industry.”

“… Yet, the United States has run a persistent, substantial, and growing trade deficit in autos and parts with Mexico for over 30 years,” the U.S. trade representative stated.

“In 2024, that deficit peaked at [US] $138.2 billion. In recent years, analysis indicates that the share of U.S. content within Mexico’s automotive exports to the United States has been declining, while the share of Chinese or other Asian content in those goods has been increasing.”

In the July 1 report, the USTR stated that the North American automotive industry “has faced external supply chain shocks, increased competitive pressures from China, and evolving U.S. trade policy.

“Further, evidence shows that U.S. content in vehicles produced in Mexico and Canada is declining, while automotive trade deficit with Mexico remains persistently large. The 2026 USMCA Joint Review will provide the United States the opportunity to assess and strengthen the USMCA automotive ROOs to incentivize the use of additional U.S. and North American content,” the USTR said.

“… In 2017, industry estimated 85 percent of the auto parts content for vehicles built in Canada originated in the United States, and more than 60 percent of the auto parts content of vehicles assembled in Mexico originated in the United States. But in 2024, industry reported that the estimated U.S.-origin content of vehicles built in Canada and Mexico dropped to 50 and 35 percent, respectively,” Greer’s office stated.

In an article published on Wednesday under the headline “U.S. insists on strengthening USMCA rules of origin,” the newspaper El Economista wrote that the USTR was seeking to bolster automotive ROOs in the three-way trade pact even though the rules are already “the strictest of any trade agreement in the world.”

In its report, the USTR noted that the USMCA “raised regional value content (RVC) requirements to 75 percent for passenger vehicles and light trucks, compared to 62.5 percent under the NAFTA,” the North American Free Trade Agreement that was superseded by the USMCA in 2020.

In accordance with the USMCA, clearing the 75% RVC threshold is one necessary condition for the tariff-free trade of vehicles within North America. However, U.S. President Donald Trump — who is determined to protect and grow the U.S. auto industry — last year imposed 25% tariffs on vehicles made in Mexico and Canada. The U.S. content in those vehicles — but not regional content — is exempt from the tariff, lowering the effective duty for most cars exported to the U.S. from Mexico.

Despite the United States’ decision not to extend the USMCA until 2042, the free trade pact remains in effect.

However, it is now set to be reviewed on an annual basis until 2036, although the three signatories can decide at any time to extend it for an additional 16 years.

Mexico-US trade talks continue in CDMX

The focus on possible changes to automotive ROOs in the USMCA comes as Mexican and U.S. officials engage in USMCA review talks in Mexico City. Mexico’s top USMCA negotiator, Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard, is already participating in the bilateral discussions, which began Monday, and Greer is set to join them.

“Ambassador Jamieson Greer will travel to Mexico from Wednesday, July 22, to Friday, July 24, to continue bilateral discussions related to the Joint Review of USMCA,” the USTR said in a statement last week.

“During the bilateral meetings, Ambassador Greer and Secretary Ebrard will discuss a range of topics including steel and aluminum and derivative products, automobiles, economic security, labor, agriculture, and electronic payment services,” the USTR said, noting also that Greer will meet with President Claudia Sheinbaum at the National Palace. That meeting is scheduled for this Thursday.

One of Mexico’s main aims in its negotiations with the United States is to secure the reduction — if not the elimination — of U.S. tariffs that currently apply to Mexican vehicles, steel and aluminum. Among the measures the Mexican government has taken that could help it secure concessions from its northern neighbor is the imposition on Jan. 1 of new and higher tariffs on imports from China and other countries with which it doesn’t have free trade agreements. The government reported on Monday that the new tariffs approved by Congress in December 2025 had reduced imports across 1,463 product categories by 23.2% between January and May. The most impacted country is China.

Segundo día de trabajos con el equipo de USTR , vamos avanzando. pic.twitter.com/pHKvZp6olF — Marcelo Ebrard C. (@m_ebrard) July 22, 2026

Underscoring the United States’ desire to strengthen automotive ROOs in the USMCA, Greer said on Wednesday that doing so was a “key objective,” according to reporting by the news agency Reuters.

However, the U.S. trade representative, who appeared before the U.S. Senate Finance Committee in Washington, D.C., before departing for Mexico, said that the resolution of the automotive ROOs issue would “take a little more time” and involve discussions with U.S. Congress “in the following year.”

However, Greer said he hoped to strike ​some interim trade agreements with Mexico and Canada this year, according to Reuters.

“We are moving with all due speed on this,” he said.

Reuters reported that Greer “did not specify what separate ‘potential interim arrangements'” with Mexico and Canada “would look like, but said he wanted ​to have options for Trump, Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to consider by the end of this year.”

Sheinbaum said last Thursday that at this week’s talks with the U.S., Mexico would be aiming to “reach some agreements that give us greater stability in the coming years.”

She has stressed that “at any time,” Mexico, the United States and Canada can agree to extend the USMCA for 16 more years, something that the Mexican and Canadian governments wanted to do this month but which the Trump administration rejected.

Mexico and the United States are each other’s largest trade partners, while Canada is the second-largest market for Mexican exports. Most trade between Mexico and the United States occurs tariff-free under the USMCA, which governs North American trade worth around $2 trillion annually.

With reports from El Economista and Reuters

World.title: Cueva twins dominate Zapopan Diving Cup, cinching gold over China for the first time ever
World.content:
Mexico has long excelled in diving, and the latest gold-medal triumph of the 14-year-old Cueva twins from the Bajío state of Jalisco demonstrates the country’s potential.

Mexican divers finished their participation in the 2026 Zapopan Diving Cup, held between July 16 and 19, with 10 medals: three gold, four silver and three bronze. Mía and Lía Cueva Lobato defeated Chinese partners Shan Lin and Yiping Long to win gold in the synchronized 3-meter springboard final, marking the first time the duo had defeated Chinese competitors in an international competition.

Mexico’s Rut Páez and Yunuen Parra finished in fourth place in the same event.

“I felt very happy,” said Lía Cueva after receiving her gold medal. “It’s the first time we’ve beaten the Chinese, and it gives us a lot of motivation to do it again at the Olympic Games.”

“We know we still have a lot of work to do, but I’m convinced that we will continue training very hard so that results like this… become more and more frequent and visible,” added Mía Cueva. “They can expect us at the Olympic Games.”

The win followed previous success at the World Aquatics Diving World Cup in Jalisco’s capital of Guadalajara, held in April 2025, in which the Cueva twins took silver in the women’s 3-meter synchronized springboard final.

Meanwhile, Mexicans Randal Willars and Kevin Berlín delivered a strong performance on the men’s synchronized 10-meter platform, beating Great Britain and Colombia to take the gold medal, with a score of 414.72 points.

In the women’s 10-meter platform event, Mexico’s Suri Cueva took the silver medal, with 303.10 points, while Samantha Jiménez took bronze with 302.15 points. China’s Zhixin Qu took first place with 369.40 points.

The Metropolitan Aquatic Center hosted representatives from nine countries in preparation for the Santo Domingo 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games, to be held from July 24 to August 8. On Monday, President Sheinbaum presided over an official send-off for the more than 600 athletes who will compete across disciplines including diving, archery, gymnastics, boxing and more.

With reports from Cronica and Grupo Animal

World.title: México state security strategy has slashed homicides in half: Wednesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

📍 Mañanera held in Toluca: President Sheinbaum took her Wednesday press conference to Toluca, capital of México state, Mexico’s most populous state with around 17 million residents.

President Sheinbaum took her Wednesday press conference to Toluca, capital of México state, Mexico’s most populous state with around 17 million residents. 📉 Homicides down sharply in México state: National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 2.8 homicides per day in the state in June, a 58% drop compared to September 2024. She said a “unified command” strategy launched in 15 high-crime municipalities last year contributed to the decline.

National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 2.8 homicides per day in the state in June, a 58% drop compared to September 2024. She said a “unified command” strategy launched in 15 high-crime municipalities last year contributed to the decline. 📅 Lowest homicide rate in 19 years: Figueroa said México state saw an average of 2.9 homicides per day in the first half of 2026, down 31% from 2025’s daily average and 68% below the 2013 rate.

Figueroa said México state saw an average of 2.9 homicides per day in the first half of 2026, down 31% from 2025’s daily average and 68% below the 2013 rate. 👮 Over 3,300 arrests since Sheinbaum took office: Security Minister García Harfuch said 3,367 people have been detained for high-impact crimes in México state since October 2024, alongside seizures of 1,219 kg of drugs and 819 firearms.

Security Minister García Harfuch said 3,367 people have been detained for high-impact crimes in México state since October 2024, alongside seizures of 1,219 kg of drugs and 819 firearms. 🎯 No timeline on Iván Archivaldo Guzmán capture: Asked how close authorities are to detaining the Chapitos faction leader, García Harfuch declined to speculate, instead pointing to the recent killing of an alleged Culiacán plaza boss as a sign of progress against the faction.

Asked how close authorities are to detaining the Chapitos faction leader, García Harfuch declined to speculate, instead pointing to the recent killing of an alleged Culiacán plaza boss as a sign of progress against the faction. ⛓️ El Mayo’s prison transfer uncertain: Asked whether Ismael Zambada could serve his life sentence in a Mexican prison, García Harfuch said that would depend on whether Mexico’s Attorney General’s Office pursues extradition, though a transfer appears unlikely.

Why today’s mañanera matters

President Claudia Sheinbaum held her Wednesday morning press conference in Toluca, capital of México state.

Located in central Mexico, the state, commonly abbreviated as Edomex, is Mexico’s most populated with just under 17 million residents when the last census was conducted in 2020.

A good number of the state’s 125 municipalities are located in the greater metropolitan area of Mexico City. They include two municipalities that are among the 10 most populated in the country: Ecatepec (1.64 million residents in 2020) and Nezahualcóyotl (1.07 million).

México state is also home to popular tourism destinations including the Teotihuacán archeological site and the magical towns of Valle de Bravo and Malinalco.

Security in the state — Mexico’s fifth most violent in the first half of the year in terms of total homicides — was a key focus at today’s mañanera, with officials presenting the latest data on homicides and arrests.

Like the vast majority of Mexico’s 32 federal entities, México state has seen a significant reduction in its homicide rate this year. Thus, federal and state officials, including Governor Delfina Gómez, who attended today’s mañanera, have statistics to back up their argument that their security initiatives are working.

Beyond the presentation of the latest security statistics, Sheinbaum’s Wednesday morning press conference was significant as Security Minister Omar García Harfuch responded to questions about Iván Archivaldo Guzmán Salazar, a Sinaloa Cartel leader and son of convicted drug lord Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, and about Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada, a Sinaloa Cartel kingpin who on Monday was sentenced to life in prison in the United States.

Homicides decline significantly in México state

National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa told reporters that the security strategy in México state has prioritized “intelligence, coordination and the territorial presence” of security forces.

She noted that a specific “unified command” strategy was implemented in 15 high-crime municipalities in eastern México state in March 2025, contributing to a reduction in homicides in the state that borders Mexico City to the north, east and west.

Figueroa presented data that showed that there was an average of 2.8 homicides per day in México state in June, a reduction of 58% compared to the daily average in September 2024, the final month of the presidency of Andrés Manuel López Obrador.

She also reported that the homicide rate in México state in the first six months of 2026 was the lowest in the past 19 years. There was an average of 2.9 homicides per day between January and June, a reduction of 31% compared to the daily average across 2025.

Compared to 2013, when there was an average of 9.1 homicides per day, the reduction in the first six months of this year was 68.1%.

Figueroa noted there was an average of 116.1 reported high-impact crimes per day between January and June, a reduction of 19% compared to 2025. Among the offenses classified as high-impact crimes are murder, kidnapping, extortion and violent robbery.

More than 3,300 arrests in México state since Sheinbaum took office

At the start of his presentation, García Harfuch said that “México state is an example of how the coordination between the three levels of government yields results.”

The security minister also said that since the current government took office in October 2024, it has worked closely with the México state Attorney General’s Office and Security Ministry “to develop investigations, carry out joint operations and detain those who generate violence in the entity.”

“This coordinated work,” García Harfuch said, has resulted in the arrest of 3,300 people who allegedly committed high-impact crimes.

Data he presented showed that the exact number of people arrested between Oct. 1, 2024, and June 30, 2026, was 3,367.

In addition, authorities seized 1,219 kilograms of drugs and 819 firearms in the same period.

“These results reflect a strategy based on intelligence and investigation, but above all operational coordination that has allowed us to disrupt criminal structures, provide faster assistance [when crimes are committed], … detain priority targets and strengthen the safety of Mexican families,” García Harfuch said.

Are authorities closing in on Iván Archivaldo Guzmán?

A reporter for the newspaper Milenio noted that Milenio recently published a report stating that Iván Archivaldo Guzmán, leader of the Chapitos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, is in a “situation of tactical vulnerability and extreme isolation.”

“How close is the security cabinet to detaining Iván Archivaldo?” the reporter asked García Harfuch.

“In order not to speculate and say how close or how far [we are from detaining Guzmán], I prefer to talk about the progress the security cabinet has made [in Sinaloa],” the security minister said.

García Harfuch noted that an individual nicknamed “El Texas” — an alleged plaza chief in Culiacán for the Chapitos — was recently killed in a clash with the army in the Sinaloa capital.

The slain man, identified in media reports as Cristhian Guadalupe Pérez Pérez, was one of the “main generators of violence in Culiacán and this entire area,” the security minister said, referring to Sinaloa.

“He was a key person for this organization, for this criminal leader,” he said, referring to Iván Archivaldo and the Chapitos.

García Harfuch said that federal security forces carry out operations in Sinaloa every week “to continue weakening” the Chapitos and “the other faction of the Sinaloa Cartel.”

He was referring to the Mayos faction, which is engaged in a long-running and extremely bloody feud with the Chapitos that intensified after Joaquín Guzmán López, another son of El Chapo, kidnapped El Mayo in July 2024 and forced him onto a private plane that flew him to New Mexico where he, and Guzmán López, were detained by U.S. authorities.

Could El Mayo be transferred to a Mexican prison?

The same Milenio reporter highlighted that Zambada’s lawyer, Frank Pérez, said in an interview that his client wants to serve his prison sentence in Mexico. He asked García Harfuch whether a transfer to a Mexican prison was possible.

The security minister said that the Federal Attorney General’s Office would have to determine whether or not it would seek the extradition of Zambada, who was also wanted in Mexico when he was arrested in the U.S. two years ago.

A transfer of the 76-year-old drug trafficker to a prison in Mexico appears extremely unlikely.

Joseph Nocella Jr., U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, said Monday that Zambada would “spend the rest of his life in a U.S. prison, exactly where he belongs.”

El Chapo, who founded the Sinaloa Cartel with El Mayo and others, escaped twice from prison in Mexico, once in a laundry cart in 2001 and again in 2015 via a tunnel that connected to his cell. He is now serving a life sentence in the Florence Supermax prison in Colorado.

World.title: União Progressista Becomes Brazil’s Biggest Congress Bloc
World.content:
By subscribing you agree to our privacy policy . We never share your email.

Politics

Key Facts —The federation. União Brasil and the Progressistas (PP) merged into a single federation, União Progressista, cleared by Brazil’s top electoral court on 26 March 2026. —The size. It commands the largest bloc in the lower house, with 109 federal deputies, plus about 15 senators — the biggest force in Congress. —The reach. The alliance also groups six governors, more than 1,300 mayors and nearly 12,400 city councillors nationwide. —The money. Together they claim the largest share of Brazil’s public party and campaign funds among 29 registered parties. —The tilt. The bloc leans toward the opposition ahead of the 2026 election, straining União Brasil’s uneasy place in President Lula’s government.

Brazil has a new heavyweight. União Progressista, a federation of two large centre-right parties, now controls the biggest bloc in Congress — and it is positioning itself against President Lula ahead of the 2026 vote.

Brazil’s National Congress in Brasília. The new União Progressista federation now holds the largest bloc in both chambers. (Photo: Cayambe / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0)

Brazil’s Congress just gained a giant. On 26 March 2026, the country’s electoral court approved a federation joining two of its biggest parties, União Brasil and the Progressistas, into a single force called União Progressista.

Overnight, it became the largest bloc in the legislature — and a headache for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

What a “Federation” Means in Brazil

A federation is far more than an election pact. Under Brazilian law, parties that federate must act as one in Congress and at the ballot box for at least four years.

That makes União Progressista much stickier than the loose coalitions that usually shift with each vote in Brasília. The two parties are now, in practice, one.

The rule was designed to curb Brazil’s party sprawl, nudging its dozens of parties into fewer, larger groupings. União Progressista is the most dramatic result so far.

Coalitions in Brazil are notoriously fickle, forming and dissolving around individual votes. A federation locks its members together, giving leaders rare certainty about who they command.

The Biggest Bloc in Congress

The numbers are formidable. In the 513-seat Chamber of Deputies, the federation fields 109 members, the single largest caucus; in the 81-seat Senate it counts around 15.

Its footprint runs well beyond the capital. The alliance groups six state governors, more than 1,300 mayors, 186 state legislators and nearly 12,400 city councillors.

By comparison, Lula’s own Workers’ Party controls a far smaller caucus, which is why the new bloc’s arrival reshapes the arithmetic of governing.

Together the two parties also hold ministries, state governments and a vast base of local officials — the kind of grassroots machine that wins elections in a country of some 200 million people.

Why Size Buys Power

In Brazil’s fragmented Congress, no president can govern without stitching together a broad majority. The largest bloc becomes the essential partner — or the most dangerous adversary.

União Progressista’s scale gives it leverage over committee chairs, the legislative agenda and the confirmation of key appointments.

It also hands the group the biggest slice of the public money that finances parties and campaigns — a decisive edge in a country where television time and campaign funds are shared out by size.

Size shapes who runs the powerful committees and sets the legislative calendar, posts from which a bloc can help or hobble a president at will.

A Tilt Toward the Opposition

The federation has signalled it will lean against Lula. That is awkward, because União Brasil has held posts in his government even as its leaders pull away.

ACM Neto, União Brasil’s national vice-president, has argued openly that the party should quit the Lula administration and back its own opposition candidate in 2026.

The bloc already carries presidential ambition. Ronaldo Caiado, the governor of Goiás and a declared candidate, sits inside it, giving the federation a horse in next year’s race.

Even so, the federation’s stance is not fully fixed. Its leaders have kept options open, wary of committing entirely to either Lula or the Bolsonaro camp before the 2026 field is clear.

For Lula, the risk is concrete: a bloc this large can slow or sink his bills, and its drift into open opposition would shrink his room to govern in a difficult final stretch.

The Tensions Inside

Bigness brings friction. União Brasil and the Progressistas have overlapping strongholds and rival local bosses who must now share candidacies and funds.

The parties are not fully aligned on 2026 either. Some figures flirt with the Bolsonaro camp; others guard ties to the very government they are supposed to be leaving.

Holding such a sprawling group together through a national election will test its leaders as much as its opponents.

The Progressistas, long a pragmatic party that tends to back whoever holds power, and União Brasil, with its own presidential dreams, do not always want the same thing.

What Foreigners Should Watch

For outsiders, the takeaway is that Brazil’s centre-right has consolidated into a single, durable machine just as the 2026 contest begins.

It shifts the balance in Congress against Lula and could shape everything from tax and spending bills to who ultimately challenges him for the presidency.

For investors, a stronger, more disciplined centre-right could mean a Congress more receptive to market-friendly bills — or simply a higher price for the government’s cooperation.

Whether União Progressista becomes the launchpad for a serious presidential bid, or simply a toll-gate that extracts concessions from whoever governs, is the question the coming year will answer.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is União Progressista?

It is a Brazilian party federation joining União Brasil and the Progressistas (PP). Approved by the electoral court on 26 March 2026, it forms the largest bloc in Congress and must act as a single party for at least four years.

How big is the União Progressista bloc?

It holds 109 seats in the 513-member Chamber of Deputies — the largest caucus — plus about 15 senators, six governors, more than 1,300 mayors and nearly 12,400 city councillors.

Why does it matter for the 2026 election?

The federation controls the biggest share of Congress and of public campaign funds, and it is leaning toward the opposition. That gives it heavy influence over Lula’s agenda and over who challenges him in 2026.

World.title: Salvadoran Fintech Ábaco Lands US$53 Million Seed
World.content:
Latin America · Business

Key Facts —Company. Ábaco, a Salvadoran digital factoring fintech for small and medium enterprises. —Round size. US$53 million in a seed round mixing equity and debt commitments. —Earlier backing. A US$4 million pre-seed round drew six venture funds, including Mercy Corps Ventures and Invariantes Fund. —Mezzanine note. Pomona Impact Fund II provided a US$2 million mezzanine debt investment in March 2025. —Regional push. Capital targets expansion from El Salvador into Guatemala and Costa Rica.

Ábaco, a Salvadoran fintech that turns unpaid invoices into same-day working capital for small businesses, has closed a US$53 million seed financing round, giving the company fresh fuel to expand its digital lending platform across Central America.
