World.title: Iraq’s public debt stands at 47% of its GDP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi prime minister’s financial advisor Mazhar Saleh told Rudaw News on Wednesday that Iraq’s total public debt is approximately 47 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).

Although Baghdad can easily handle its debt burden, the country’s dependency on revenues generated from oil exports leaves its economy exposed to various external factors.

The major issues in the Iraqi economy, according to Saleh, are its reliance on oil income, the poor performance of other productive sectors, and the growing administrative costs.

To guarantee that the Iraqi economy can survive foreign shocks, the Iraqi government is working to diversify income sources, notably in the industrial, agricultural, and service sectors, as well as reforming the tax, customs, and banking systems, according to Saleh.

In late June, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed that the country’s domestic debt rose to 95.7 trillion Iraqi dinars ($73 billion) by the end of April 2026 compared to 90.51 trillion dinars ($69.1 billion) recorded at the end of 2025, representing an increase of 5.16 trillion dinars ($3.9 billion).

In 2024, the domestic debt in Iraq stood at 83.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $63.4 billion).

According to the statistics, domestic debt increased during the first four months of 2026, while external debt dropped in comparison to prior years.

Iraq’s external debt stood at $54.101 billion in 2025, compared to $54.601 billion in 2024 and $56.207 billion in 2023, marking a total drop of $2.106 billion over two years, according to the CBI.

Senior officials in the Iraqi financial sector and representatives from Oliver Wyman, a renowned firm specializing in financial audits, emphasized the significance of developing medium-term plans customized to the nature of the debt, Iraq’s credit rating, and key global indicators.

The officials also called for drawing up budgets based on realistic evaluations of the country’s available finances and execution capabilities.

World.title: Iraqi security seizes 40 gold bars, large sums of cash in corruption case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council revealed on Wednesday that investigations into the case of Adnan al-Jumaili, a deputy oil minister accused of corruption, have resulted in the seizure of 13 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $10 million), $400,000, and 40 gold bars hidden in different locations in the northern province of Salah al-Din.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s ongoing nationwide anti-corruption campaign launched last month.

The Iraqi judiciary said in a statement that each of the gold bars weighs one kilogram. It added that security forces also seized five kilograms of gold jewelry, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

The seizures resulted from ongoing investigations into the suspect, according to the statement.

Al-Jumaili’s case is one of the most prominent corruption cases that emerged in the past few months, as the government’s campaign targets people suspected of theft and wasting public funds.

Iraqi authorities had already announced al-Jumaili’s arrest on allegations of financial and administrative corruption before the judiciary opened a broad investigation into the issue, including a review of his accounts, assets, and finances.

The Supreme Judicial Council did not provide any information on the locations where the money and gold were discovered and mentioned that search and recovery efforts are ongoing.

The Iraqi cabinet affirmed that recovering public funds is one of the priorities of its agenda, while the Federal Commission of Integrity and the judiciary are working to pursue those accused both inside and outside Iraq.

World.title: Air defenses intercept 4 drones in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The international coalition’s air defense systems intercepted on Wednesday evening four drones over Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The systems were activated when flying objects approached the US consulate and its associated logistics base, according to Al-Arabiya News.

Four explosions were reportedly heard in the skies over Erbil following the activation of the international coalition’s air defense systems.

A security source confirmed that air defenses successfully intercepted and destroyed the drones before reaching their targets, adding that the attack caused no casualties or material damage.

On Tuesday, Iraqi security sources said that air defenses intercepted three explosive-laden drones near the US consulate in Erbil with two drones targeting a camp of the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group.

The state-run news agency (INA) reported that Erbil International Airport temporarily suspended flights but later announced their resumption.

Iraqi air defenses shot down an explosive-laden drone on Monday near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US and international coalition forces. There were no reports of casualties or damages.

No group has claimed responsibility for the attacks. Neither Iraqi officials nor the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has issued a statement identifying the attackers or the types of drones involved.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: US dollar rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,504 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,502.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,510 Iraqi dinars and 1,500 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,508.5 and 1,507.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi proposes joint fund in call with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held high-level telephone discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, focusing on expanding economic cooperation, trade, and industrial investment between the two nations.

According to an official statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the talks covered bilateral ties across multiple sectors, with particular emphasis on economic partnerships, trade volume expansion, direct investment, and joint migration management frameworks.

Key Discussion Pillars

Joint Iraqi-German Fund: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi proposed establishing a dedicated joint fund to finance industrial development projects in Iraq with German technical and capital backing.

Economic Reforms & Anti-Corruption: Al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s commitment to eradicating administrative corruption and creating an open, transparent environment for foreign capital to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

Official Invitation to Berlin: Chancellor Merz extended a formal invitation to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi to visit Germany for an official state visit to deepen economic and political coordination.

Support for Fiscal Reform: Germany reaffirmed its support for the Iraqi government’s ongoing economic and financial reforms, expressing strong readiness from German corporations to expand investment footprints across Iraq.

The discussions highlight Baghdad’s broader diplomatic strategy of leveraging European economic integration to modernize domestic industrial infrastructure and broaden trade partnerships beyond energy exports.

World.title: Lebanon PM says Beirut working for ‘complete Israeli withdrawal’
World.content:
Zawtar al-Gharbiyah – Lebanon is working towards a “complete Israeli withdrawal” from areas it occupies, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday on a visit to a village where Lebanon’s army recently deployed.

“We will continue mobilising our political and diplomatic efforts to secure a complete Israeli withdrawal from the south,” he said in Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

Israeli forces were previously present on the outskirts of the village following the war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Salam visited the town a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House, where he “stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon’s army is meant to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from “pilot zones” where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.

Hezbollah has repeatedly rejected the agreement and refuses to lay down its weapons.

The military said on Tuesday that Israeli forces “opened fire” near troops deploying at Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

The Israeli military said it had only fired “warning shots into the air” after Lebanese soldiers entered an area that was “not part of the pilot area”.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Tehran on March 2, prompting major Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion.

After planting a Lebanese flag in Zawtar al-Gharbiya on Wednesday, Salam said “in parallel with the army’s deployment, we will continue opening roads, removing rubble, and securing essential services, enabling our people to return safely and with dignity to their homes and villages”.

– ‘Heads held high’ –

The war caused widespread destruction, mainly in the south, though violence has declined since the signing of a framework agreement between the United States and Iran last month and the Lebanon-Israel deal.

According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 people have returned to their homes over the past few weeks.

In Zawtar al-Gharbiya, dozens of residents waited at the village’s entrance for permission to go check on their homes.

“We will enter the town with our heads held high, thanks to the presence of the Lebanese army,” Abbas Yaghi, 73, told AFP.

The military had told residents on Tuesday to avoid entering the village “until the security situation stabilises”.

The army is conducting a sweep of the town, which is geographically contiguous with its Israeli-occupied neighbour, Zawtar al-Shariqya.

Israeli troops still launch intermittent strikes in surrounding towns, the latest on Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

“We will follow the army if it gives us permission to enter,” Mostapha Ammar, a 60-year-old resident of Zawtar al-Sharqiya said, hoping that Israel would withdraw from other areas.

Wafaa Ismail, 64, also from Zawtar al-Sharqiya, was not granted permission to enter the neighbouring village as Salam visited.

She expressed frustration at seeing the prime minister enter on his own, escorted by the army, saying: “He should have brought the people in with him so he could claim victory.”

World.title: Ukraine’s new army chief: who is Mykhailo Drapaty?
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky has announced Mykhailo Drapaty as the country’s new commander-in-chief, following a political crisis triggered by Zelensky’s surprise ousting of a young modernising defence minister.

The 43-year-old Drapaty replaces Oleksandr Syrsky, 60, an accomplished military strategist but who was long criticised for Soviet-style practices and not caring about human losses.

Here is what we know about Drapaty.

– Fighting Russian separatists –

Drapaty is a career military officer trained exclusively inside Ukraine’s independent, post-Soviet system.

He began as a lieutenant and rose through the ranks, shooting to nationwide fame during the war with Russia-backed separatists in 2014.

In a video which went viral, he commanded an infantry vehicle as it smashed through a makeshift barricade set up by pro-Moscow forces in the southern city of Mariupol.

Recalling the incident in an interview with Ukrainian media, Drapaty said his driver asked: “Major, there are barricades ahead. What do we do?”

“I said, ‘Dima, step on the gas'”.

The vehicle, with the blue-and-yellow Ukrainian flag affixed to its top, then smashes through the tyre-and-barricade wall, leaping into the air and speeding on.

During the fight with Moscow-backed rebels, Drapaty is also credited with re-capturing several settlements from Russian control and then saving his unit from being encircled.

Drapaty has a wife and kids, Ukrainian media reported.

– Backing army ‘transformation’ –

Drapaty is seen as a consensus candidate and popular choice.

He enjoys a good reputation within the military, and protesters calling for his predecessor’s removal often chanted his name as their preferred replacement.

Despite being well-known, he has kept a low profile and only rarely given interviews — in contrast with many other Ukrainian commanders.

After a string of Russian attacks on Ukrainian training grounds, he resigned from his position as ground forces commander in June 2025 — a move that set him apart as commander willing to take responsibility for mistakes.

“If we fail to draw conclusions, to change our attitude toward service, to acknowledge our mistakes, we are doomed,” he said at the time.

“That episode illustrates his decisiveness and strong ethical standards,” political commentator Volodymyr Fesenko told AFP on Wednesday.

Drapaty was immediately moved to become head of Ukraine’s joint forces command, from where he pushed for reforms inside the system.

After the dismissal of moderniser Fedorov last week, he said the “transformation” of the army must continue.

“When the right decision has to be implemented in spite of the system, rather than because of it, it means that the system itself needs to change,” he said in a rare public intervention.

“The army needs new rules,” he added.

– Hailed as ‘fresh air’ –

His nomination was hailed by many inside and outside the army.

The appointment is “wonderful news”, said Sergiy Prytula, the head of one of Ukraine’s biggest charities supporting the military.

“This is a breath of fresh air and a new hope in the struggle of free people for freedom and justice,” the ousted defence minister Fedorov, an ally, said on social media.

In Moscow, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the change would not impact the course of the war.

“I don’t think this will lead to any changes on the front lines,” he told reporters, adding that Moscow intends to continue pressing on with its almost four-and-a-half-year offensive.

– Facing a ‘very difficult time’ –

Despite Ukraine being in one of its best positions on the front line in months, Drapaty faces serious challenges.

The army has been blighted by several scandals — particularly over an unpopular mobilisation drive, the treatment of conscripts and reports of widespread absenteeism and equipment shortages in some units.

“The new Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine will have a very difficult time. Much harder than he imagines,” former army chief Valery Zaluzhny — removed in 2024 — said.

The public row over the last week has exposed hidden divisions within Ukraine’s military and political leadership.

His appointment, seen as an attempt to bridge the divide, carries heavy expectations.

“Appointments made against a backdrop of social turmoil always come with many pitfalls,” said Prytula, adding that Drapaty now faces “inflated expectations”.

World.title: Iraq signs $200 billion in deals with US energy companies
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said on Tuesday that the deals struck with US energy corporations during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States are estimated at $200 billion.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the new agreements will raise Iraq’s oil production capacity, create job opportunities, and help the country achieve self-sufficiency in gas by 2030, according to the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The deals include agreements with HKN Energy, Chevron, and Halliburton to develop the oilfields of Hamrin, West Qurna-2, Nasiriyah, Balad, Bin Omar, and Sindbad, as well as an agreement with Syria to construct the Haditha-Baniyas oil pipeline.

Khudair noted that Iraq’s current oil production capacity is 4.8 million barrels per day, but the government is in serious discussions with the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) to increase oil exports.

Just like most other oil producers, Iraq has to face the issue of how to attract investments and increase production under the restrictions imposed by OPEC.

Despite having some of the world’s greatest crude oil reserves, ongoing production constraints impede Iraq’s efforts to generate revenues needed to support its growing population.

World.title: 'Sent four formal proposals': MoS Jitendra Singh invites protesters for talks at JP Nadda's place
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister Jitendra Singh on Thursday invited the protesters against NEET paper leak for talks at JP Nadda's place on the central government's behalf. This comes after the talk on Monday with the Cockroach Janta Party's spokespersons failed to bear any results.

"I wish to share that in the last 24 hours as many as four offers were made to the student representatives for a dialogue. It is my humble appeal to the students on agitation that the government is ready for talks whenever you want, at whichever hour of the day and for as much length of time that you wish to," he said.

"We are ready to discuss the issue on which the agitation has happened, and all the other related issues as well.

The talks can be held with an open mind at the residence of Union health minister JP Nadda and of course I will be accompanying him. The talks could be held at Nadda's residence or at the office, or whichever of the two you wish to," he added.

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that he had ordered for setting up of fast-track courts "to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks."





"Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps in this regard. This continues our series of steps for safeguarding the interests of students. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," he said in a post on X.

World.title: ‘You take credit for Mars, now take responsibility': Priyanka Gandhi targets PM Modi over student protests, police action
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP

Vadra on Thursday launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the ongoing student protests, accusing him of taking credit for the country's achievements while refusing to accept responsibility for the concerns of young people.

Speaking to reporters in Parliament, Priyanka alleged that students protesting over the alleged NEET paper leak and related issues had been subjected to police action, and questioned the government's handling of the demonstrations.

Priyanka questions PM over police action on students

Referring to Prime Minister Modi's social media post earlier in the day, Priyanka said there was a contradiction between the government's stated concern for students and its actions on the ground.

"He takes credit for going to Mars, he takes credit for every achievement which is the achievement of our youth and the achievement of our people. He takes credit, doesn't he? So now is the time for him to take responsibility for his actions," she said.

Alleging that students were lathi-charged and tear-gassed during the protests, she added, "Modi ji is responsible for our youth feeling that there is no future. Modi ji is responsible if our children who are demonstrating...





he is tear-gassing them and having them lathi-charged. If something happens to even one of them, it is his responsibility."

Questioning reports of internet restrictions in parts of central Delhi, Priyanka asked, "Are we living in a democracy? Students are not terrorists. Their parents would be worried, their families would be worried, they cannot contact anyone."

Earlier in the day, she also urged the Centre to engage with the protesting students, saying they had "lost faith in the system".

Speaking to news agency ANI, she said the government should address their demands, including the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and action over the alleged assault on protesters.

"He is a leader, and the time has come to show leadership. Listen to the demands of the students... If you have faith in the students, then why are the students being lathi-charged? If you are worried about the students, then call and speak with them," she said.

PM announces fast-track courts as Parliament protests intensify

Priyanka's remarks came hours after Prime Minister Modi issued his first public response to the ongoing agitation, announcing that the government would set up fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for those involved in paper leak cases.

"Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared,"

wrote on X.

The controversy continued to dominate the Monsoon Session of Parliament, where NDA and INDIA bloc MPs staged rival protests outside Parliament over the NEET issue and the Opposition's demand for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

Tensions briefly escalated at Makar Dwar as MPs from both sides confronted each other, prompting Parliament security personnel to form a human chain to separate the two groups.

BJP leaders accused the Opposition of avoiding a debate on the issue, while Congress leaders maintained that accountability must begin with the resignation of the education minister.

World.title: India's dying rivers: How our cities are choking their lifelines
World.content:
NEW DELHI: "Nature provides enough to satisfy every manâs needs, but not every manâs greed.â The words widely attributed to Mahatma Gandhi perhaps resonate nowhere more starkly today than along Indiaâs rivers.

From Delhi to Mumbai, Chennai to Hyderabad and Bengaluru, India's urban rivers tell similar stories. They have been straightened, narrowed, encroached upon and increasingly turned into conduits for the waste generated by constantly expanding cities. Rivers that once shaped settlements now survive by carrying sewage.

Yet every river has paid a different price.

The Yamuna has lost much of its width to floodplain encroachments and water diversion.

A recent study found that the river, which flows through the northern and southern stretches of the national capital and is also known as the Kalindi, has shrunk by nearly 68% over the past 220 years.

If the Yamuna is struggling, the Sahibi River in national capital has already crossed the brink and is now ecologically degraded, according to Central Water Commission report of Jal Shakti ministry.

Sahibi River in Delhi

Once an important seasonal river flowing through western Delhi, the Sahibi has gradually disappeared beneath urban expansion.





Today, most residents know it simply as the Najafgarh drain or nala, a heavily polluted water channel carrying black sewage through the city.

Meanwhile, Mumbai's Mithi river has been reduced to a storm-water drain overwhelmed by unchecked urban development. Hyderabad's Musi and Chennai's Cooum now carry far more sewage than freshwater, while Bengaluru's Vrishabhavathi has effectively become the city's wastewater channel.

Even the mighty Brahmaputra in Northeast, relatively cleaner than most urban rivers, is steadily losing land to relentless erosion as climate change and urban pressures continue to mount.

Together, they reveal a common truth: India's cities have grown by steadily reducing the space available for rivers.

Delhi: Yamuna that lost its floodplain



No river illustrates this transformation more dramatically than the Yamuna.

A recent study by researchers from Delhi University and the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER), Bhopal, found that the Yamuna's average width through Delhi has shrunk by nearly 68%, from about 658 metres in 1799 to roughly 210 metres today.

Water discharge has fallen by almost 90%, largely because of barrages, canals and diversion projects.

The researchers also argue that shrinking floodplains have made Delhi more vulnerable to flooding. Embankments have confined the river to an increasingly narrow channel, helping explain why the capital witnessed record floods in 2023 despite lower river discharge than during the 1978 floods.

The Yamuna has long occupied centre stage in Delhi's political discourse.

Every election brings renewed promises to clean the river, with rival parties blaming each other for its deteriorating condition.

Yet, despite repeated assurances, the river remains heavily polluted and is often described as being on the brink of becoming biologically dead.

Its condition is impossible to ignore. As it winds through Delhi, the Yamuna carries dark, polluted water choked with untreated waste.

Downstream, it reaches Agra, where it flows beside one of the world's greatest monuments -- the Taj Mahal.

The contrast between the pristine marble monument and the foul-smelling river has become an uncomfortable reminder of India's environmental challenges.

Agra: Garbage lines the polluted banks of the Yamuna near the Taj Mahal

During US President Donald Trump's visit to the Taj Mahal in 2020, authorities even released additional water into the Yamuna to improve its appearance.

Mumbai: When a flood exposed a dying Mithi river



For Mumbai, it took a disaster.

The catastrophic floods of July 26, 2005, which claimed over 500 live, exposed what decades of urban expansion had done to the 17.8-km Mithi River.

According to the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), suburban development over the past 25 years has "drastically degraded" the river's water quality. Once an important natural storm-water channel, the Mithi now carries untreated sewage, industrial effluents, municipal waste and sludge.

Wetlands and floodplains have disappeared under roads, industrial estates and the Bandra-Kurla Complex.

Encroachments have narrowed the river, reducing its ability to carry monsoon runoff.

Although the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation said that widening and retaining-wall works have doubled storage capacity and tripled carrying capacity since 2005, officials admit pollution remains the biggest challenge.

The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board identifies untreated sewage, industrial discharge and solid waste as the principal reasons behind the river's continued degradation.

The BMC and MMRDA have undertaken widening, deepening, desilting, construction of retaining walls and pollution-control works along the river.

The largest municipal body in country, BMC has said that retaining wall construction is nearly complete, while MMRDA is implementing sewage interception and an odour-control pilot project aimed at improving dissolved oxygen and reducing pollution.

The renewed desilting and anti-encroachment initiatives after the alleged desilting scam were also reported.

Hyderabad: Musi river flowing mostly on sewage



The Musi tells perhaps the clearest story of a river losing its natural identity.

The Telangana government's Musi Riverfront Development Corporation said the river now runs "nearly dry" through Hyderabad because reservoirs upstream, catchment degradation and urban encroachments have drastically reduced natural flows.

What remains is largely sewage.

The Union environment ministry classifies stretches of the Musi among India's "Priority-I polluted river stretches", while the ministry of Jal Shakti said four sewage treatment plants with a combined capacity of 593 MLD have been created under the National River Conservation Plan.

Even so, untreated wastewater continues entering the river through multiple nalas or drains as Hyderabad continues to expand its stretches and grow into a full-fledged metropolitan area.

The state now proposes a 55-km riverfront restoration project centred on complete sewage interception, ecological restoration and flood management, an acknowledgement that beautification alone cannot revive a river whose biggest problem is pollution.

Chennai: Cooum river reduced to urban sewer



The story of the Cooum is equally sobering.

Flowing about 65 km, the river once supported transport and recreation before becoming overwhelmed by Chennai's urban growth.

Government data cited in Parliament records Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) levels of 105 mg/litre in the Cooum -- among the highest for India's urban rivers. Healthy river water typically records BOD below 3 mg/litre.

Under the National River Conservation Plan, projects worth Rs 404.25 crore created 264 MLD of sewage treatment capacity through four treatment plants, according to environment ministry.

However, the project includes both Cooum and Adyar rivers.

Yet Cooum's untreated sewage continues entering the river through multiple drains.

A Comptroller and Auditor General audit mentioned that Tamil Nadu itself described the Cooum as "an urban sewer due to drainage of municipal and industrial waste."

The Chennai River Restoration Trust has cleared encroachments, relocated thousands of families and restored stretches near Island Grounds.

But officials continue to acknowledge that stopping sewage inflows remains the key challenge.

Bengaluru: Vrishabhavathi river carrying city's waste downstream



If Hyderabad's Musi resembles an open drain, Bengaluru's Vrishabhavathi has effectively become one.

The Central Pollution Control Board describes the river as acting as "a drain for domestic and industrial wastewater."

Flowing into the Byramangala reservoir before joining the Arkavathi, the river carries much of Bengaluru's treated and untreated sewage downstream.

CPCB has repeatedly directed Karnataka authorities to strengthen sewage treatment, improve industrial effluent management and protect floodplains.

Heavy rainfall frequently transports garbage and plastic downstream. Residents near Bidadi have complained that truckloads of Bengaluru's waste accumulate around bridges after every major spell of rain.

The river illustrates how pollution generated inside one city increasingly affects communities far beyond municipal boundaries.

Assam: A different kind of shrinking Brahmaputra river



The Brahmaputra also nurtures some of the Northeast's fastest-growing urban centres. From Dibrugarh to the bustling metropolis of Guwahati, cities have risen and continue to expand along the banks of the mighty river.

Unlike India's urban rivers, the Brahmaputra's greatest challenge is not just sewage.

It is erosion.

Every year, villages, farmland and public infrastructure disappear as one of the world's largest braided rivers shifts course.

Recognising the scale of the problem, the Centre and the Asian Development Bank signed a $200-million agreement in 2024 to strengthen flood and erosion management across 650 km of the river in Assam.

The Assam government documents described erosion as one of the state's biggest developmental challenges. Protection works continue around vulnerable areas such as Majuli, while future planning increasingly relies on satellite imagery, GIS mapping and hydrological modelling.

Although pollution levels remain far lower than those in India's metropolitan rivers, officials warned that urbanisation and untreated sewage around cities such as Guwahati are emerging concerns.

The Brahmaputra demonstrates that shrinking rivers are not always about pollution. Sometimes, rivers lose land while people lose homes.

The Brahmaputra's relentless erosion and annual floods continue to threaten millions in the Northeast.

Fed by heavy monsoon rains, the river frequently swells beyond its banks, leaving large parts of the region inundated.

Ganga: A river struggling under weight of India's cities



If the Ganga is India's most revered river, it is also among its most stressed. Flowing through some of the country's fastest-growing cities, including Haridwar, Kanpur, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Patna and Kolkata.

The Ganga faces a different challenge. Unlike the Yamuna, its biggest burden stems from industrial pollution, compounded by religious offerings, ritual waste, funeral remains and the enormous crowds that gather during events such as the Mahakumbh.

For centuries worshipped as "Maa Ganga" and celebrated as a symbol of purity, the river today ranks among the world's most polluted waterways.

The river has increasingly become a victim of urban expansion, pollution and shrinking natural floodplains.

As cities have grown, the Ganga's floodplains have steadily disappeared beneath roads, residential colonies, commercial developments and embankments. These encroachments have narrowed the river's natural corridor, reducing its ability to spread during the monsoon, recharge groundwater and sustain wetlands.

Pollution remains the river's biggest challenge. Despite significant investments under the Namami Gange programme under PM Modi-led government, untreated sewage from expanding urban centres continues to enter the river through hundreds of drains.

Industrial effluents, particularly from leather tanneries, sugar mills, distilleries and textile units, add to the pollution burden, although regulatory enforcement has improved in recent years.

During the lean season, reduced environmental flows due to barrages and water diversion further limit the river's ability to dilute pollutants.

Large-scale restoration efforts have expanded sewage treatment capacity, intercepted drains and improved riverfront infrastructure in several cities. Yet government assessments continue to emphasise that engineering projects alone cannot revive the Ganga.

More than water, a test of India's cities



Taken together, these rivers tell a remarkably similar story despite their different geographies.

Some have been narrowed by embankments. Others have lost wetlands, floodplains and natural channels to highways, commercial districts and housing colonies. Many now receive more sewage than freshwater.

Governments have invested thousands of crores in programmes such as Namami Gange, the Yamuna Action Plan, the National River Conservation Plan and city-specific restoration projects. New sewage treatment plants, riverfronts and desilting drives are important interventions.

But almost every official report arrives at the same conclusion: rivers cannot be revived by engineering alone.

Unless untreated sewage is intercepted, floodplains are protected, encroachments are prevented, and ecological flows are maintained, India's rivers will continue to shrink-even if they appear cleaner on the surface.

The question is no longer whether India's cities need rivers. They always will. The real question is whether India's cities can continue to grow without taking away the very space that allows rivers to remain alive.

World.title: 'Considerable time:' Private airport operators flag BCAS clearance delays with Govt
World.content:
Some examples of how it took to get BCAS nod:



The longest wait. 802 days: Central kitchen at Bengaluru T2

664 days: New casualty centre at T1, Mumbai

635 days: Interim floor plan vetting at T1, Kochi

448 days: Converting Delhi Airport T1 Pier C from domestic to international

340 days: Terminal building plan phase-I, Navi Mumbai

The fastest nod. 7 days: Strengthening perimeter wall at IGIA

NEW DELHI: In an unprecedented move, Indiaâs private airport operators have warned that âconsiderable time being taken in processing security vettingâ is âimpacting project implementation schedules, achieving operational efficiencies, commercial preparedness, and ensuring passenger convenience. â The Association of Private Airport Operators (APAO), which represents the 14 PPP airports in India including those in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and represents a lionâs share of air traffic in the country, has written to aviation secretary Samir Sinha on the need for âtimely approvalsâ Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS).APAO has sent to Sinha a list of projectsâ along with the time it took for them to get BCAS clearance, which ranges from a week to 802 days. The longest time (802 days) has been taken for approving âcreation of central kitchen at T2â Bengaluru. Nod for a ânew casualty centre facility at T1 CSMIA (Mumbai)â took 664 days; Kochi airportâs âinterim floor plan vettingâ took 635 days; clearing alternate location for isolation bay at Delhiâs IGIA took 578 days; the nod for IGIA T3 pier Câs conversion from domestic to international took 448 days and âterminal building plan phase 1 of Navin Mumbai Airportâ took 340 days.Comments were sought from the aviation ministry on the APAO mail and awaited till the time of going to press. BCAS is an âattached organisationâ of the ministry.Operators of these 14 airports â Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Kochi, Delhi, Goa (Mopa), Hyderabad, Guwahati, Jaipur, Lucknow, Mangalore, Mumbai CSMIA, Navi Mumbai, Thiruvananthapuram and Greater Noida â have requested the ministry to âestablish turnaround timelines for different proposal categories to facilitate faster processing of proposals critical for operational continuity and passenger service enhancement. â The operators include the Adani Group, GMR and other private players.A former senior official of BCAS said both the operators and the authority were equally to blame for delay in big projects. âBigger proposals have to e examined in totality from security aspect and we seek clarifications from them regarding the same which are often slow to come by. Then there is too much commercialisation at newer terminals and security is very often not the key consideration while designing those layouts. Then background checks of personnel means sending the same to IB. How long it takes there is beyond us. Most bigger proposals have foreigners as partners, so that takes even longer.âHowever, the former official admitted that clearance for smaller things, like say a shop, should come faster and that is where BCAS can speed up. âThatâs why there is an e-portal where applicants can check the status of their application and see if it is stuck, why so and provide the required inputs. On smaller proposals, BCAS can do better.âThe mail written by APAO secretary-general Satyan Nayar says: ââ¦.considerable time being taken in processing security vetting approvals for various infrastructure, operational, and reconfiguration proposals submitted by APAO member airports. As airports continue to witness significant passenger and cargo growth, utmost important to undertake timely capacity enhancements, improve passenger facilitation, ensure operational optimization, and augment security infrastructure projects. ââFor all this to happen, timely approvals from BCAS becomes highly critical for ensuring smooth execution of these activities and achieve operational readiness. However, it has been observed that a significant number of proposals across member airports are experiencing prolonged timelines at various stages of security vetting approvals.ââIn several cases, approvals pertaining to the design stage, final stage and floor plan stages have remained under process for extended durations, thereby impacting project implementation schedules, achieving operational efficiencies, commercial preparedness, and ensuring passenger convenience,â the mail adds.(Source: APAO letter)

World.title: 9 Indian fishermen held by Sri Lankan navy for alleged illegal fishing
World.content:
At least nine Indian fishermen on Thursday were arrested and their trawler seized by the Sri Lankan Navy for allegedly fishing illegally in the island nation's waters.

According to the Navy, the fishermen had crossed the International Maritime Boundary Line and were apprehended while fishing north of Talaimannar.

The fishermen were apprehended on Wednesday evening during an operation after the Sri Lankan Navy detected more than 50 Indian fishing trawlers allegedly crossing into Sri Lankan waters south of Iranativu and engaging in illegal fishing, according to an official statement by the navy cited by PTI.

The nine arrested fishermen and the seized trawler were handed over to the Fisheries Inspector in Mannar for further legal proceedings.

The latest arrests come amid persistent tensions over the fishermen issue between India and Sri Lanka. According to Sri Lankan authorities, 128 Indian fishermen had been arrested and 18 trawlers seized for alleged poaching in the island nation's waters as of April 15 this year.

The fishermen issue remains a longstanding point of contention in bilateral ties, with the Sri Lankan Navy repeatedly detaining Indian fishermen and seizing their boats for allegedly crossing into its territorial waters.





There have also been instances in which Sri Lankan naval personnel have opened fire on Indian fishermen in the Palk Strait.

The Palk Strait, a narrow stretch of water separating Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka, is a rich fishing ground used by fishermen from both countries. Arrests are frequent as fishermen often inadvertently cross the International Maritime Boundary Line while fishing.

World.title: 'Found no evidence': CBI gives clean chit to kingpin Sanjeev Mukhiya in NEET-UG 2024 paper leak case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Thursday said it found no evidence linking alleged paper leak kingpin Sanjeev Kumar alias Sanjeev Mukhiya to the theft or distribution of the NEET-UG 2024 question paper, despite his initial inclusion as an accused in the FIR registered by Bihar Police.

In a statement, the agency said Bihar Police had named Mukhiya in the FIR after the NEET-UG paper theft was detected in 2024, citing his alleged involvement in other examination paper leak cases. However, after the case was transferred to the CBI, the agency conducted a detailed investigation and identified all those involved in the theft, distribution of the stolen question paper and the beneficiaries.

The CBI said it filed multiple chargesheets against 45 accused before a Patna court but did not find any evidence to establish Mukhiya's role in the NEET-UG 2024 paper leak conspiracy.

"Mukhiya remained absconding during the relevant period and was later arrested by Bihar Police. Since he was named in the FIR, the CBI took him into police custody for examination in the NEET-UG 2024 case. However, no evidence of his involvement emerged during the investigation," the agency said.

As a result, the CBI did not name Mukhiya in any chargesheet in the case, following which he secured bail in the NEET-UG 2024 matter. The agency added that he continued to remain in judicial custody in connection with other cases being investigated by Bihar Police.

The CBI maintained that its probe had identified the entire conspiracy behind the NEET-UG 2024 paper theft and ensured that all those involved were brought to justice.

World.title: Dhaka appointment of press officer could lead to another flashpoint in ties
World.content:
The government under Tarique Rahman's leadership has appointed a young journalist as Minister (Press) at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi. The appointee, journalist Saidur Rahman, has previously made social media posts critical of India and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, questioned India's role in Bangladesh's 1971 Liberation War, and called for the release of convicted war criminal ATM Azharul Islam following the political transition in Bangladesh.

It is learnt that the Indian government is following the development closely and is yet to approve the appointment of Rahman who had also accused India of destabilising Bangladesh. This follows a the diplomatic row last month over a visit to India by another top Bangladesh official, Zahed ur Rahman.

The official had flown out of the Delhi airport in a huff, after a dispute with immigration authorities who held him for âverificationâ because of his controversial statements about India in the past.

According to Indian authorities, Zahed he had been allowed a one-time exemption to enter India but he still chose to return.

Saidur Rahman, currently Political and Election Affairs Editor at the Daily Ittefaq, has been appointed Minister (Press) at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi.

In a now-deleted social media post, screenshots of which continue to circulate online, Rahman alleged that India had staged "drama" in the name of cooperation during Bangladesh's 1971 Liberation War and referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks describing December 16, 1971, as a historic victory for India.





"As a Bangladeshi, I declare in clear language that 1971 was our own war of independence. Our prideâ¦.the great freedom achieved in exchange for the blood of millions of martyrs and the honor of mothers and sistersâ¦the ropes of Indian slavery were broken and that freedom was fulfilled on August 5, 2024. Today we are free. We did not accept the tyranny of Pakistan or India, nor will we. We are Bangladeshis. Our country is Bangladesh," he wrote.

In another social media post (now deleted), Rahman claimed that a new political force had emerged to perpetuate Indian hegemony. Referring to the 2009 BDR mutiny, he wrote: "On February 25, 74 people, including 57 army officers, were martyred in Peelkhana in the tragic BDR mutiny. It is alleged that the fascist Awami League, fueled by India, killed smart army officers."

He also wrote: "ATM Azhar must be released."

According to a gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Public Administration on Sunday, Saidur Rahman has been appointed on a contractual basis for a one-year term, effective from the date of his joining.

The post had remained vacant since the departure of journalist Faisal Mahmud in February, after his contractual appointment was cancelled.

Mahmud, who had been appointed by the then interim government, served as Minister (Press) for nearly nine months.

World.title: 'Stringent action against guilty': Amit Shah breaks silence on NEET leak, backs fast-track courts
World.content: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday said the welfare and future of the country's youth remain the Modi government's "highest priority and resolve". Shah endorsed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's decision to set up fast-track courts for speedy trials in examination paper leak cases.The announcement comes amid continuing protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which has demanded the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak controversy.In a post on X, Shah said, "The welfare of the youth and their bright future is both the highest priority and the resolve of the Modi government. The decision to expedite hearings and take stringent action against the guilty in paper leak cases through the establishment of fast-track courts by the Prime Minister is a reflection of this very commitment."Calling the move a landmark step, Shah said it would be a "milestone" in cracking down on those who "toy with the future of the youth due to paper leaks".Shah's remarks came hours after PM Modi announced the government's decision to establish fast-track courts to deal with examination paper leak cases, marking his first public response after days of protests by students demanding accountability over recurring leaks.In a post on X, the PM said, "Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth!"He added that the concerned authorities and officials had been directed to take all necessary steps in this regard, saying the move was part of the government's continuing efforts to safeguard the interests of students.Meanwhile, demonstrations intensified in New Delhi on Wednesday night, where protesters briefly clashed with police as security personnel used tear gas and batons to disperse the crowd. The issue has also disrupted proceedings in Parliament, with Opposition parties demanding the resignation of the Pradhan and raising the matter repeatedly during the Monsoon Session.Bharatiya Janata Party leader Nitin Nabin also reiterated the government's position, saying it remained committed to protecting students' interests.Meanwhile, protests continued in the national capital along with several parts of teh country, with student groups demanding systemic reforms and greater accountability over competitive examination leaks.

The call for a Parliament discussion on the NEET paper ‘leak’ issue, and the demand for Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation, again took centrestage today in both Houses on day 4 of the ongoing Monsoon Session. World.title: BDA puts checks on builders seeking plan modifications in Bengaluru
World.content:
In a move aimed at protecting the interests of flat owners in apartment complexes, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) has issued a detailed circular laying down strict guidelines for approving modified building plans after the issuance of Occupancy Certificates (OCs).

The BDA has made it clear that no modified building plan can be sanctioned once the permissible Floor Area Ratio (FAR) has been fully utilised and an Occupancy Certificate has been issued for the entire project. Once the final OC is granted, builders will permanently lose the right to seek modifications to the sanctioned building plan.

In cases where only a partial occupancy certificate has been issued, and permissible FAR remains unutilised, builders may seek modifications. However, the original sital area, parks, open spaces, and civic amenity areas shown in the first sanctioned plan cannot be altered.

Third-party rights

The circular further mandates that if third-party rights have already been created through the sale of flats, builders must obtain the consent of at least two-thirds of the purchasers before seeking any modification to utilise the remaining FAR.

The circular will likely put an end to developers illegally using increased FAR to construct additional buildings for extra profits. For instance, Aleem, a resident of Kanakapura Road, said that his apartment complex was constructed in 2003, and the OC was issued in 2006. The undivided shares were also transferred subsequently. However, with the expansion of the Metro, the FAR in the area increased significantly. “The developer obtained a modified sanctioned plan from the BDA, and constructed an additional building on the same land,” he said.

The construction was allegedly approved without obtaining the mandatory consent of at least two-thirds of the apartment owners, as required under the Karnataka Ownership Flats Act, 1972 (KOFA), and the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA).

Modified plans not allowed if... The permissible FAR has been fully utilised All Occupancy Certificates (OC) have been issued Key Conditions Original sital area cannot be altered Parks, open spaces and civic amenity areas cannot be changed for construction Vacant land not earmarked for future development cannot be used Two-thirds consent of flat owners mandatory if apartments have already been sold Balance FAR and TDR can be utilised only if future development is disclosed in sale deeds/agreements Additional construction should not alter the Undivided Share (UDS) of apartment owners Once the final OC is issued, the builder permanently loses the right to seek approval for modified building plans

Mandatory NOC

The BDA has also directed that any future utilisation of balance FAR, Transferable Development Rights (TDR), or Premium FAR must have been explicitly disclosed in the sale agreements or deeds executed by the developer. Additional construction will also require mandatory No Objection Certificates (NOCs) and approvals from all competent authorities.

To safeguard flat owners’ rights, the authority has specified that any additional construction undertaken by utilising balance FAR or TDR should not alter the undivided share (UDS) of land belonging to purchasers.

The circular also states that vacant land not earmarked for future development in the original sanctioned plan cannot be considered while approving modified plans. Further, while processing such applications, the town planning and engineering sections must verify whether any part of the project has already received an occupancy certificate.

Integrated platform

To streamline approvals and eliminate communication gaps between departments, the BDA has proposed developing an integrated software platform linking the Town Planning and Engineering Sections. An Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system is to be developed within six months and implemented from April 1, 2027.

The authority has also fixed a timeline of 90 days for disposing of applications submitted to the town planning and engineering sections, requiring officials to either approve or reject them within the stipulated period.

World.title: Kerala professor’s arrest in BDS student’s death raises larger questions on safeguards against ‘illegal’ arrests
World.content:
Larger questions surrounding personal liberty and the legal safeguards available to citizens against illegal arrests without a warrant have come into renewed focus in Kerala with the recent “illegal” arrest of Dr. Kodanda Ram, a former faculty member at the Dental College, Anjarakandy, Kannur.

Dr. Ram was arraigned as an accused in the case booked in connection with the alleged suicide of Nithin Raj, a first-year BDS student, on April 10, 2026. Dr. Ram, who went into hiding for 101 days after being slapped with the provisions of the Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, was arrested by the police and produced before the Sessions Court, Thalassery, recently.

However, M. Manoj, the Principal Sessions Judge, set the accused at liberty after finding that Mr. Ram was arrested by the police “in complete disregard” of the Constitutional provisions and the safeguards for personal liberty set by the Supreme Court.

The violations of the mandatory provisions and fundamental rights prescribed by the Constitution in the case came to light on an interaction of the sessions judge with the accused.

The accused, when asked whether he was informed about the grounds of arrest, told the court that he was arrested because the student committed suicide. The lawyers for the accused also informed the court that the police had not conveyed the grounds of arrest, and that he was not provided with the reasons for the arrest in writing, as stipulated by the Supreme Court in a few landmark judgments.

The absence of the mandatory compliance of the directions of the Supreme Court to furnish the grounds of arrest in writing breached the fundamental rights of the accused and violated the legal safeguards against illegal arrest, as provided by the apex court, observed the trial court, while ordering him to be released forthwith. The police, which released him from custody, subsequently arrested him, after apparently providing him in writing the reasons for the arrest.

The court found that the information provided to the accused about the reasons and grounds for the arrest was also insufficient. The reasons were merely mentioned as: “the accused had committed a serious offence and the anticipatory bail of the accused was rejected by the Supreme Court,” which were grossly inadequate and failed to uphold the spirit of the apex court order, the trial court found.

The non-compliance of the constitutional requirement and statutory mandate would lead to the custody or detention being rendered illegal, the trial court held, while quoting elaborately from the judgments of the apex court.

In one of the landmark judgments, the apex court held that the grounds of detention should be “effectively and fully communicated to the arrestee in the manner in which he will fully understand the same.” The court further explained that the “grounds of arrest must be informed in a language which the arrestee understands.”

In yet another case, the court held that the “mode of conveying the grounds of arrest must necessarily be meaningful so as to serve the intended purpose.” The effective and full communication of reasons for the arrest is also required for the arrestee to exercise his constitutional right, as specified in Article 22 (1) “to consult an advocate of his choice and the right to be defended by an advocate. If the grounds of arrest are not communicated to the arrestee, as soon as may be, he will not be able to effectively exercise the right to consult an advocate,” the court pointed out.

Fundamental right to liberty

The fundamental right to liberty, guaranteed under Article 21, gets curtailed when a person is arrested. “When such an important fundamental right is curtailed, it is necessary that the person concerned must understand on what grounds he has been arrested. That is why the mode of conveying information of the grounds must be meaningful so as to serve the objects stated above” and the requirement of “informing the person arrested of the grounds of arrest is not a formality but a mandatory constitutional requirement,” the sessions judge noted, referring to the apex court verdicts.

The court further cited a Supreme Court verdict that “if the grounds of arrest are not informed immediately after the arrest, it would amount to a violation of the fundamental right of the arrestee guaranteed under Article 22 (1) and deprivation of the arrestee of his personal liberty.”

If there is a “failure to comply with the requirement of informing the grounds of arrest soon, the arrest is vitiated. Once the arrest is held to be vitiated, the person arrested cannot remain in custody even for a second,” the court observed.

The sessions court also went harsh on the investigating officer in the case with its observations that the “investigating officer, who arrested the accused, has disregarded the directions of the Supreme Court of India, which mandates furnishing the grounds of arrest and reasons for arrest to the accused in a meaningful manner and which is his constitutional right.”

The omissions on the part of the investigating officer amounted to disregarding the directions of the Supreme Court and dereliction of duty, observed the sessions judge. The court also ordered a notice to the investigation officer to explain why the Supreme Court guidelines of informing reasons for arrest and grounds of arrest were not complied with in letter and spirit in the case.

Meanwhile, Justice A. Badharudeen of the Kerala High Court has sought a report from the trial court regarding the developments, while expressing concern in the manner in which the police had arrested the accused. The judge has also sought the personal appearance of the police officials concerned before the court on Friday (July 24, 2026).

World.title: Body of Kerala’s Kottayam native missing in Sikkim tunnel accident recovered
World.content:
The body of a geologist from Kottayam district in Kerala who went missing after a landslide inside an under-construction tunnel in Sikkim has been recovered.

The deceased has been identified as Aneesh Mohan, 43, of Pathazhakkuzhy, Velloor, near Pampady, in Kottayam. Family members, who travelled to Sikkim, have identified his body. According to relatives, the body was discovered around Wednesday midnight (July 22, 2026) and will be flown to New Delhi after a postmortem examination. From New Delhi, it will be brought to his ancestral house near Pampady via Nedumbassery.

A Senior Manager and Geologist with the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC), Aneesh had been working at the organisation for the past 16 years. Posted to Sikkim from Haryana seven months ago, he was part of the team tasked with assessing the rock strata at the tunnel construction site, including their geological stability and water content.

July 20 accident

The accident occurred on Monday (July 20, 2026) inside a 7-km-long tunnel which was under construction in Namchi district as part of Stage IV of the Teesta Hydroelectric Project.

The family learnt about the incident after an NHPC official contacted the Head of the Department of Geology at Government College, Kottayam, where Aneesh had studied, seeking the family’s contact details. The NHPC officials also informed Aneesh’s brother, Bineesh, who is based in Abu Dhabi, and subsequently arranged for Aneesh’s wife, Sangeetha, and Bineesh to travel from New Delhi to Sikkim by air.

Aneesh completed his Bachelor’s degree in Geology from Government College, Kottayam, between 2001 and 2004, and obtained his Master’s degree from the same institution between 2004 and 2006. He joined the NHPC in Haryana in 2011 and had been living there with his family before being posted to Sikkim.

He is survived by his wife, Dr. Sangeetha, children Arnav and Karthyayani, who are now residing in Tripunithura; and his parents, P.K. Mohanan and Amminikutty.

World.title: Social activist Anna Hazare undertakes 'maun andolan' to support protesting students
World.content:
Social activist Anna Hazare on Thursday (July 23, 2026) observed a two-hour-long maun andolan (silent protest) at Ahilyanagar in Maharashtra to extend his support for protesting students in Delhi.

“Anna began his protest at 11 a.m. and ended it at 1 p.m.,” the social activist’s aide Datta Awari told PTI.

Jantar Mantar protest LIVE

Mr. Hazare, who held the protest at the Mahatma Gandhi statue in Ahilyanagar, later left for his village, Ralegan Siddhi, located in the same district.

Mr. Hazare wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday (July 22, 2026), saying “the news of…violence and police action…is extremely painful”.

In a letter to Mr. Modi, Mr. Hazare said the resentment of the protesters must be viewed “not as a law and order problem, but as the agony and expectations of society”.

If Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan is asked to resign, “it will not cause the government to fall; rather, it will…make its functioning more accountable and effective”, Mr. Hazare wrote.

He requested the government to “listen to [the protesters] patiently, create an atmosphere of trust, and find solutions through positive dialogue”.

World.title: Israelis fear Saudi nuclear deal could ignite West Asia arms race
World.content:
A deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia allowing the kingdom to ​build nuclear reactors using American technology and to enrich uranium ‌has fuelled fears in Israel of the start of ​an arms race in the West Asia.

The agreement, ⁠which still needs Congressional approval, that was announced on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) is meant to allow the Saudis to develop a civilian nuclear programme.

Prime ‌Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Defence and Foreign Ministers have so far not commented on ‌the deal, which critics say compromises Israel’s long-term security ‌interests.

“The ⁠nuclear agreement that is coming together with ⁠Saudi Arabia, over Israel’s head, is a serious strategic failure that endangers our security,” said former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who is seeking to unseat Mr. ​Netanyahu in an October ‌27 election. “Nuclear enrichment on Saudi soil could lead to a regional nuclear race and a dangerous loss of control.”

Former Defence Minister Avigdor Lieberman said that “the civilian nuclear program ‌in Saudi Arabia will end in nuclear weapons and ​will lead to a crazy arms race throughout the entire Middle East (West Asia).” Israel, which is widely ⁠believed to have the region’s only nuclear arsenal, must oppose the deal and lobby Congress to stop the deal, he ‌said.

A civil nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia has been in the works for years during both President Donald Trump’s first administration and that of former President Joe Biden. No deal has come together before now, however, in part because of warnings from non-proliferation groups who say that ‌it could offer Saudi Arabia a path to develop a nuclear ​weapon.

Israelis also had hoped any deal would come as part of a long-sought normalisation agreement between ⁠Israel and the Saudis, as envisioned in the Biden plan. “There is ⁠no security official who would say that introducing civilian nuclear capability into Saudi Arabia without integrating the ‌move as part of building a moderate regional alliance is a step that is good for Israel’s ​security,” said Benny Gantz, a former Defence Chief.

World.title: NHAI revises toll charges on Bengaluru-Nelamangala and Bengaluru-Kolar highway stretches
World.content:
Toll charges on the Bengaluru-Nelamangala stretch of NH-48 and the Bengaluru-Kolar section of NH-75 have gone up from Wednesday, following the National Highways Authority of India’s (NHAI) revision of user fee rates for the financial year 2026-27.

According to separate public notices issued by the Project Implementation Unit (PIU), Bengaluru, the revised toll rates will be applicable at the Bengaluru-Nelamangala toll plazas on NH-48 and the Hedaginabele, Agrahara, Krishnarajapura and Sundarapalya toll plazas on the Bengaluru-Bethamangala section of NH-75.

On the Bengaluru-Nelamangala access-controlled highway, the toll is collected at six locations. For cars, jeeps, vans and light motor vehicles, the single journey toll ranges from ₹10 to ₹35, depending on the toll plaza. The highest charge of ₹35 is applicable at TP-1, while TP-2 has the lowest charge of ₹10. Return journey and monthly pass charges have also been revised across all categories of vehicles.

Meanwhile, on the Bengaluru-Kolar highway, revised toll rates have been notified for four toll plazas. For cars and other light motor vehicles, the single journey fee is ₹50 at Hedaginabele and Agrahara, ₹120 at Krishnarajapura and ₹150 at Sundarapalya. Users travelling across multiple toll plazas will pay cumulative toll based on the distance covered.

The revised tariff also applies to commercial vehicles, buses, trucks and multi-axle vehicles, with corresponding increases in return journey and monthly pass charges. The annual pass for eligible vehicles has been fixed at ₹3,075 for 2026-27.

The NHAI stated that the revised user fee has been notified under the provisions of the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008, as amended, and is based on the annual revision mechanism prescribed under the rules. The revised rates came into effect from 00:00 hours on July 22, 2026, according to notification.

World.title: ‘Just don’t judge’: Sister Tina defends Kushal Tandon after Shreya Kalra’s DM accusations
World.content:
Actor Kushal Tandon, currently seen on Amazon Prime Video’s reality show Alliance, has been making headlines for his conduct on the reality show. While Kushal has been accused of bullying and manipulating his fellow contestants, his personal life has also come under the spotlight on social media. In an exclusive interview with SCREEN, Kushal’s sister Tina Tandon defended his behaviour on the show. She also responded to allegations made by actress and content creator Shreya Kalra on Lock Upp Sach Ya Sazaa.

Defending Kushal’s behaviour on the show, Tina said, “You are locked in the house 24/7. Reality shows put you under immense pressure. They have no family or friends, so at times it just gets very heavy. We see the edited version of 54 minutes. There we see someone get triggered or overwhelmed with emotions. That’s common, and it happened with Kushal also. You guys are seeing Kushal as someone who is upfront on reality shows. I have known him all my life. He is the same person in and out. Kushal stands by his values and loyalties. For him, friendships matter the most; game comes second. It was the first time we also saw him breaking down. Imagine the pressure he must have been under. He felt suffocated. Reality shows test your patience.”

Also Read: Kushal Tandon-Vanshaj Singh fight on Alliance leaves Sohail Khan fuming: ‘Fail to understand’

Tina then shared how the family felt seeing Kushal break down after his showdown with Vanshaj. She said, “Seeing him break down affected us a lot. At home, my mom was in tears for two days. She was like, ‘This is enough.’ But TV shows a one-hour episode. You don’t know if he was singing a song after that moment. Yesterday when I went to see him, he was happy. Alliance is an amazing, classy show. At the end, they are all friends. Things happen in the heat of the moment.” Tina visited Kushal during the show’s family week. Talking about her visit, Tina said, “It was very sudden. I was not supposed to go inside. Kamya Panjabi was supposed to be there. I just requested to meet him, but that was not allowed, and then I just went. It was so overwhelming. I couldn’t see anything around me, just him in front of me. He did get a little emotional. We met very nicely. He was shocked to see me.”

Tina Tandon on Kushal Tandon’s negative image

Kushal Tandon’s behaviour on Alliance has been a frequent topic of discussion among contestants and on social media. Addressing the negative image that has formed around Kushal, Tina said, “I have not been active on social media in my life as much as I have been now. I have seen the reels and the views about him, which were initially negative. Kushal is not fake, and he has no filter. As a person, he is genuine and won’t befriend people just for the game. He is saying things on people’s faces and is misunderstood. Personally, Kushal is also like this. If he gets angry, he will be angry. If you explain something to him, he will say sorry too. Sohail sir is like a big brother to him, which makes him calmer. People who are making him negative are doing so from their perspective, which is formed from a 50-minute edited episode. On a reality show, there are 150 cameras where some people get away with being fake. Kushal cannot do that. He is like that at home too. He is not manipulative.”

Tina further said Kushal has remained true to himself on Alliance despite the backlash. “Kushal keeps his promise to the core, even if it affects his game. He is a very family-oriented and emotional person. But he gets instigated easily. If you poke him, sometimes he reacts. He loses his cool quickly, but that’s human nature, and everyone is different. He will never break a relationship if he is committed to you. Viewers should watch the show with an open mind and not judge. I am proud that my brother is emerging as a strong contender. He means no harm as a person.”

Also Read | Kushal Tandon’s sister defends him after Shreya Kalra claims he cheated on Shivangi Joshi

Tina also addressed Kushal’s equation with Sohail Khan and Ravi Kishan, saying their bond is genuine and not a part of his game plan. She said, “Everyone thinks Kushal is being nice to Sohail because he is a big man. When Kushal had the restaurant, Sohail sir had come there for its opening. He met Salman Sir too. There is respect and bonding, and he has stood by him. Everyone has been hesitant to play with Sohail, but Kushal stands with the man. If he loves somebody, he stands by them. It’s not that Kushal is nice to Sohail just because he is Salman Khan’s brother. Ravi Kishan also spoke so highly about Kushal. When he left, he gave his daughter’s responsibility to him.”



Tina on cheating allegations made by Shreya Kalra against Kushal Tandon

On Lock Upp Sach Ya Sazaa, actress and content creator Shreya Kalra claimed that Kushal Tandon had slid into her DMs while he was reportedly dating Shivangi Joshi. She said that he messaged her after they shot a promotional video for Barsatein – Mausam Pyaar Ka. Recalling the incident, Shreya said, “He DMed me after the shoot. I was dating someone at that time. At that time, there was something between Kushal Tandon and Shivangi Joshi. I didn’t know about it. He started speaking to me. I got a hunch and stopped. Then, Shivangi and I met on the set, and she was like, ‘Oh hi! Yes! He told me about you, that you followed and messaged him.’ I said, ‘Excuse me! I wouldn’t be the first person to approach any man. I’ve never done that in my entire life.’ I gave my phone to her. She read my whole chat. I didn’t flirt back, and I didn’t say anything.”

Post the revelation, Kushal’s sister Tina issued a statement social media refuting Shreya’s claims. Now, talking about the allegations, Tina said in the interview, “People only want to make up things for content. Everywhere it is Kushal. People are saying it’s Kushal’s show. He leaves an impact where he goes. Everyone talks about him. Episodes start with him, end with him, promos feature him. Technically, he is all over the place.”

She added, “We had to counter the statements she made because I felt, as a sister, I had to stop these speculations because they are not true. I know because I have his phone. I also know him as a person. Let him come out. Just don’t judge a person when he is not even here. People have been making assumptions that he ditched her or whatever the relationship happened. We didn’t want another speculation for no reason. On Alliance, we let go of things. People asked us to do paid PR, but we said no. As a person, Kushal would never do these things. As his family, we also don’t want to give money for paid collaborations. We have never done it. For this content, I had to speak up because reels were being made. We had to stop one piece of content, which is wrong and unnecessary. We are there to defend him, and I was prepared to get the bashing. I cannot see his image go here and there for something he hasn’t done. Just because people say things for TRP doesn’t mean we have to believe them. You cannot act so dumb, right?”

World.title: ‘Peaceful protest is a constitutional right’: 140 HC lawyers question Mumbai Police’s prohibitory orders
World.content:
A group of over 140 lawyers practising before the Bombay High Court, including senior advocates, on Wednesday issued a statement deprecating the prohibitory orders passed by the Mumbai Police restricting movement and unlawful assembly of five or more persons in view of the recent gatherings and protests.

The lawyers sought that the Mumbai Police Commissioner withdraw the prohibitory orders, the subsequent actions by Police “to curtail lawful protests by citizens” and refrain from pursuing further action against peaceful protests.

The statement issued on July 21 claimed that no such prohibition can remain in force for more than 15 days without the State government’s sanction and that consecutive prohibitory orders (July 7 to 21 and July 23 to August 6), with only a respite of 24 hours, appear intended “to circumvent the requirement of State government sanction”.

It further said that “mass detention and arrests by the Mumbai police are also concerning” in the context of the recent prohibitory orders issued under the Maharashtra Police Act, 1951. The lawyers said constitutional courts have repeatedly held that restrictions on the right to peaceful assembly must record the facts and reasons warranting such curbs and demonstrate that they are the least restrictive measure.

Signed by at least 141 lawyers, including senior advocates Janak Dwarkadas, Navroz Seervai, Gayatri Singh, Mihir Desai, Dinyar Madon and Haresh Jagtiani, along with advocate Yug Mohit Chaudhry, the statement said the prohibitory orders “appear to fail to comply with the requirements under law”, lack accountability and create “difficulties in immediately obtaining legal redress”.

“It ought not to fall on citizens to seek recourse to already overburdened courts,” it said.

Senior advocate Dwarkadas said there was no response to lawyers’ statement urging the police authorities. “We have only made an appeal to the Mumbai CP to withdraw the ban, which appears to be without any justification. It is a clear indication that they don’t want people to assemble and protest, which is nothing but un-democratic. Right to protest is part of our right,” he told The Indian Express.



In a resolution issued Wednesday night, the Bombay Bar Association (BBA) stated that in a constitutional democracy, “the right of citizens to assemble peacefully and to express dissent is an integral facet of the freedoms guaranteed under Article 19 of the Constitution of India” and that “peaceful protest is not merely a constitutional right but an essential feature of democratic governance.”

Expressing “grave concern” over reports of students being subjected to lathi charges and tear gas by the police, it said the use of force against students exercising their constitutional rights is “deeply disturbing”. The BBA said law enforcement authorities are expected to act with restraint and noted that the right to peaceful protest is recognised by the International Covenant of Civil and Political Rights, 1966.

The Association, however, unequivocally condemned reported acts of violence, vandalism and destruction of public or private property by protesters, stating that resort to violence “cannot be justified under any circumstances”. It also deprecated intimidation tactics, including the filing of FIRs.

The BBA said the issues raised by students on the “future of education” are of “immense public importance” and deserve “meaningful engagement rather than confrontation” through “constructive dialogue” between students and the government, urging all concerned to exercise restraint, uphold the rule of law, and refrain from violence in all forms.



Referring to the Delhi High Court issuing notices, BBA President and Senior advocate Nitin Thakker told The Indian Express he did not know what judicial process in Mumbai would follow, but “strongly” condemned the use of force against peaceful protests and demonstrations. He said “citizens have a fundamental right to peaceful protest in a constitutional democracy and there was no justification for police action if protests remained peaceful.”

He referred to news reports that students protesting in Dadar, Mumbai were apprehended and detained, their phone numbers collected, threatened with criminal cases and, in some instances, booked in FIRs. “These are intimidatory tactics and this should not be at all tolerated,” he said, adding that “in a democracy, there is no such place for such kind of behaviour on the part of police when protests are peaceful.”
